  hands it to `RecordingConverter(..., speech=None)` (stored as `_speech`).

- **Media helper 1.1.0** (`agentsync.convert.media`, `media_frames.swift`; spec S7, S8 rule 1). Two verbs, as
  the fake of `tests/media_kit.py` answers them. `pills FILE --request REQ.json [--step-ms 2000]`: REQ is
  `[{"tick": k, "boxes": [[x, y, w, h], ...]}]` in fractions of the frame, origin top-left; per item the frame
  on display at `k x step` (the exact-frame generator `scan` and `frames` use), and per box the median of
  `B - R` over its pixels with `R + G + B < 600`, an integer (the lower median of an even count; 0 when no
  pixel is that dark). The box covers pixel columns `floor(x W) - 4` to `ceil((x + w) W) + 3` and rows
  `floor(y H) - 2` to `ceil((y + h) H) + 1`, clamped to the frame. Answer `{"pills": [{"tick", "values"}]}` in
  request order. `audio FILE --out DIR`: the first sound track as `DIR/audio.pcm`, 16 kHz mono 16-bit
  little-endian PCM, read from the start and never by seeking; answer `{"file": "audio.pcm", "sample_rate":
  16000, "channels": 1, "samples": N}`; no sound track is exit 3 (`the recording has no sound`). The helper
  decodes to float at the track's own rate and channel count and does the rest itself: the channels averaged,
  a Blackman-windowed sinc low-pass (16 zero crossings a side, cut at 0.47 of the lower rate) evaluated in
  Double in a fixed order, rounded to 16 bits. AVFoundation's own 16 kHz converter was dropped because it gave
  a second byte stream in 2 of about 260 runs of a 2 s clip under load. Apple's AAC decoder itself is not
  bit-exact on long files (a 10-minute 44.1 kHz file: about 1 ulp in 1.3 % of float samples, so 41 of 9.6 M
  16-bit samples off by one, and every run different), so `audio.pcm` may differ by +-1 in a few samples per
  million: nothing hashes it (no cache key, no fingerprint, no piece key); the speech result stored once as a piece
  is what pages use. `MediaEngine.pills(src, request, *, work, timeout, step_ms=STEP_MS) ->
  dict[int, tuple[int, ...]]` takes `request` as `(tick, boxes)` pairs, `Box = tuple[float, float, float,
  float]` (x, y, w, h), writes `work/pills.json`, and returns the values per tick in box order; `{}` for an
  empty request without a call, ValueError for a tick asked twice. `MediaEngine.audio(src, out, *, timeout) ->
  Audio`, `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class Audio: path: Path; samples: int`. Both validate as the
  other verbs do: the same ticks in request order, one value per box, each an int (not a bool) in -255..255;
  `audio.pcm` named so, `sample_rate` 16000, `channels` 1, and a file of exactly 2 x `samples` bytes. Anything
  else is `MediaError("the media helper's answer is not the expected JSON")`, which holds no path. The bump
  changes `MediaEngine.identity` to `media-avfoundation-h1.1.0`. Tests: `tests/test_media.py` (the fake's
  `pills` and `audio`, their bad answers, and
  `test_the_real_media_helper_reads_the_pills_and_the_sound_of_a_clip_it_made`: a clip with a 440 Hz tone, a
  blue box that reads lit and a grey one that reads 0, bytes compared over two runs).
- **The speaker cue** (`agentsync.convert.cue`, `src/agentsync/convert/cue.py`; spec S7, C18). Pure: no I/O, no
  helper call; the recording converter calls the helper and these. `CUE_REVISION = 1` (`identity()` is
  `cue-r1`, the `+cue-r<n>` mark of the converter's version); `LIT_AT = 50`: a `teams` label is lit when its
  value is 50 or more (49 is not). `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class Label: text: str; box:
  tuple[float, float, float, float]` (x, y, w, h fractions). `has_cue(profile)` is True for `teams` only in P3:
  `meet`'s cue (C18, its corner and right-tile labels) lands with P4's Meet example, as every P4 profile's cue
  lands with its own example. `requests(profile, labels, ticks)`: per tick in the order given, the labels of the
  last read candidate at or before it (`labels` keyed by candidate tick); a tick before every candidate, or
  whose last candidate read no label, is left out (an older candidate's labels are not used); `[]` for a
  profile without a cue. `lit_sets(asked, values)`: per asked tick, the texts of the labels whose value is
  `LIT_AT` or more, in box order (`values` is `MediaEngine.pills`' answer; S8b keeps these sets).
  `speaking(lit)`: `(tick, label text)` in tick order, a `SPEAKING` line where exactly one label is lit and its
  text differs from the last line's; two lit or none write nothing and do not reset the last line, so `A`,
  none, `A` is one line. `options()` carries `cue_revision`, `cue_lit_at`, `cue_widen_px` (`4,2`),
  `cue_dark_below` (600) and `cue_<profile>` per profile with a cue. Tests: `tests/test_cue.py`.

- `agentsync.convert.naming` (new, pure; spec S8b). `name_voices(voices, lit, *, profile, step_ms=2000)` takes the
  S8 voices as `Voice(number, spans)` (spans in ms, `start <= t < end`) and, per tick `k` at `k x step_ms`, the label
  texts S7 drew as speaking, and returns one frozen `Naming` per voice in number order: `number`, `form` (`named`,
  `shared`, `mixed`, `unidentified`), `label` (the most frequent, `None` without lit samples), `seen` of `lit` (`a`
  of `n_v`), `percent` (the voice's share of the label's lit samples, floored), `voices_on_label` (`k`), `held_back`,
  `gated`. A lit sample is a tick with speech of exactly one voice and exactly one label lit; a tick inside two
  voices' speech counts nowhere. In order: fewer than `N_MIN` lit samples is unidentified; `p_v < P_MIN` is mixed;
  a label under `STREAM_MIN` lit samples has no `s(L)` and is not taken; `s(L) < S_MIN` is shared (it names no
  voice, so the gate does not hold it); a voice that is not the one holding `s(L)` is unidentified; `s(L)` or
  `p_v` inside `BAND` above its floor holds the name back (unidentified, `held_back`, then `HELD_BACK_NOTE` under
  its `VOICE` line); a profile outside `CHECKED_PROFILES` (empty until the operator's B.3 listen) prints
  unidentified with `gated`, and the index's Voices block carries `GATED_NOTE` once when any voice is gated. Only a
  voice past all of these is named. Ties go by count, then label text (the holder of `s(L)` by count, then lower
  number); shares compare as exact fractions. `vetoed(naming, start_ms, end_ms, lit, *, step_ms=2000)` is the
  turn veto for one speech line of a named voice: True when the line's lit samples point at another label most
  often; the renderer then writes the window `NOTE` `veto_note(number)` at the line's time and leaves `SAID vN:`
  as it is. `voice_text(naming)` is the text after `VOICE: ` in the 3.3 forms (the grammar's `VOICE_FORMS`).
  `identity()` is `n<NAMING_REVISION>` (`n1`); `options()` holds `P_MIN`, `N_MIN`, `S_MIN`, `STREAM_MIN`, `BAND`
  and `CHECKED_PROFILES` (comma-joined, sorted) under `naming_*` keys. The floors are never tuned down (rule 7).
  No voice vector reaches this module: it sees spans and label text only.

- `agentsync.convert.speech_lines` is S8's arithmetic after the engine has run (spec S8 rules 2 and 5 to 7,
  3.5 Voices and Gaps and bounds): pure functions, no helper, no I/O. Inputs are typed by the protocols
  `WordLike` (`text`, `start_ms`, `end_ms`) and `SegmentLike` (`speaker`, `start_ms`, `end_ms`), which
  `agentsync.convert.speech.Word` and `Segment` satisfy; words are ordered by `(start_ms, end_ms, text)` and
  segments by `(start_ms, end_ms, speaker)`, so no result depends on input order. Every time is an integer ms.
  Constants: `SILENT_FRAME_MS` 20, `SILENT_DBFS` -60, `SILENT_RUN_MS` 500, `HOLE_GAP_MS` 8,000,
  `HOLE_SPEECH_MS` 4,000, `HOLE_MARGIN_MS` 5,000, `PAUSE_MS` 1,000, `SENTENCE_MS` 5,000, `LONGEST_MS` 30,000,
  `QUIET_MS` 20,000; `options()` returns each under a `speech_` key for the recording converter's options hash.
  `silence(pcm, sample_rate=16_000)` maps 16-bit little-endian mono PCM to silent runs of 500 ms or more: a
  20 ms frame is silent when every sample is 0 or `sum of squares * 10**6 < samples * 32768**2` (RMS under
  -60 dBFS, integers only); a short last frame is judged on its own samples; an odd byte count raises
  `ValueError`. `sound_ends(silent, duration_ms)` is the start of the run reaching the end, else None.
  `holes(words, segments)` returns the gaps of 8 s or more between consecutive words (from the latest word end
  so far to the next start) holding 4 s or more of all speakers' merged segments; the stretches before the
  first word and after the last are not holes. `clip_of(hole, duration_ms)` adds 5 s each side, clamped.
  `splice(words, hole, clip_words)` adds the clip words whose midpoint lies strictly inside the hole and
  returns all words sorted; clip words carry recording time (the caller adds the clip's start).
  `numbering(words, segments)` returns each word's voice (parallel to `words`) and the speaker-to-voice map:
  a word's segment is the one holding its midpoint (ends included), else the nearest, ties to the earlier
  segment then the speaker id; voices are numbered 1, 2, ... by first word, then speakers with segments but no
  word by first segment start; with no segment every word is voice 1 and the map is empty.
  `said_lines(words, voice_of)` builds `SaidLine(voice, start_ms, end_ms, text)`: a line closes at a change of
  voice, before a word starting 1 s or more after the line's latest end, after the first word ending in `.`,
  `?` or `!` whose end is 5 s or more after the line's start, and before a word that would end more than 30 s
  after the line's start; text is the words joined by one space, whitespace inside a word collapsed, and
  `end_ms` is the latest word end. `reading(words, segments, silent, duration_ms, unrecognised)` returns
  `SpeechReading(lines, voices, spans, unrecognised, sound_ends_ms, quiet, words)`: `voices` is one
  `VoiceStats(voice, speaking_ms, lines, first_ms, last_ms)` per voice, where speaking time is the sum of
  the voice's merged segment spans and first and last are its first word's start and latest word end (its
  segments' when it has no word); `spans` maps every voice to its merged segment spans (input to S8b);
  `unrecognised` is the caller's flagged gaps still empty after repair, sorted (the `speech detected, no
  words recognised until HH:MM:SS` NOTE); `quiet` is the gaps of 20 s or more in the union of segments and
  words inside `[0, sound_ends_ms)`, or the whole recording when sound never ends; `words` is the word count.

- **The transcript converter** (`agentsync.convert.vtt`, `src/agentsync/convert/vtt.py`; spec P3, section 5
  rule 5). `VttConverter` (`converter_id = "vtt-turns"`, `extensions = (".vtt",)`, version
  `1.0.0+python-<v>+unicode-<v>`, options `decode`, `max_page_bytes`, `turn_pause_ms`) is in `Registry.default`
  always (no OCR needed); `.vtt` leaves `PlainTextConverter.extensions`. It reads WebVTT as Teams, Zoom and Webex
  write it: the `WEBVTT` header block and `NOTE`, `STYLE` and `REGION` blocks skipped, cue ids optional, timings
  `HH:MM:SS.mmm` or `MM:SS.mmm` (a `,` accepted for the `.`) with cue settings ignored, `<v Name>` and
  `<v.class Name>` spans to their `</v>` or the cue's end, every other tag dropped with its text kept, and
  `&amp; &lt; &gt; &nbsp; &lrm; &rlm;` decoded once. One WHOLE unit, one line per turn:
  `[HH:MM:SS] SAID <name>: <text>`. A turn is consecutive cues of one named speaker, closed at a change of speaker
  or at a pause of 1 s or more between one cue's end and the next one's start (lead decision); cues are taken in
  start order; its time is its first cue's start floored to the second. Words under no voice tag print `SAID:`
  and are never merged. A name never holds `:`, `[`, `]` or a control character (each a space, runs collapsed);
  text and names are cleaned as the recording page cleans its own (no control, format, tag or filler character,
  lone surrogate or Unicode line break; `<` printed `&lt;`, `![` printed `!\[`, a trailing `[?]` printed `(?)`),
  so every body line begins with `[` and is one `heard` line to the curate lint (`_EVIDENCE_LINE`). The id is the
  lint's contract: a page whose `converter` starts with `vtt-turns@` is a transcript. Names are the file's,
  checked by the curate rules before use. No `WEBVTT` first line (after an optional BOM, or bytes that are not
  text) is `UnreadableSourceError("not a WebVTT transcript (no WEBVTT first line)")`; no cue with words is
  `UnreadableSourceError("a WebVTT transcript with no cue")`. Output depends on the bytes only; over
  `max_page_bytes` the body is cut at a line with the full text in `full-text.txt`.
- **Read again once.** `VttConverter.replaces = ("text-plain",)`: a converter may name the converter ids whose
  pages it makes anew. `cycle._reread_targets` adds a target for each `produced_by` record whose converter id is
  in some current converter's `replaces`, for that converter's suffixes only (so a `.txt` page of `text-plain`
  is never one: `Manifest.reread_candidates` matches the suffix), and `_lacks` answers True for a result such a
  converter id made; both read `replaces` behind the registry guard (`cycle._replaced`, as `_outdated_rule`).
  `VttConverter.outdated_key` (`"replaces text-plain"`) moves the re-read record's capability digest, so a
  source whose re-reads said done looks once more.

```python
# agentsync.convert.vtt
class VttConverter:
    converter_id = "vtt-turns"
    extensions: tuple[str, ...] = (".vtt",)
    replaces: tuple[str, ...] = ("text-plain",)
    def __init__(self, cfg: ConvertConfig) -> None: ...
    def version(self) -> str: ...
    def options(self) -> Mapping[str, OptionValue]: ...
    @property
    def outdated_key(self) -> str: ...
    def convert(self, src: Path, *, name: str) -> tuple[RenderedUnit, ...]: ...
```

- `agentsync.convert.recording` gains `Speech` and the `Reading` fields `picture_unread`, `speech`,
  `no_speech`, `speaking` and `cue_identity` (defaults keep P1 pages), and `RecordingConverter` fills them
  (spec S7, S8, S8b). **Version:** `<emitter>+<ocr>+<media>-s<n>+cue-r<n>`, plus `+<SpeechEngine.identity>-n<n>`
  with a speech engine; `options()` adds `cue.options()` always and `speech_lines.options()`,
  `naming.options()` and `recording_speech_limit` with one. `outdated_key` is
  `<emitter><<floor>|<cue identity>|<speech identity or ->`. `outdated(produced, reason)` is also True for a
  version without `+cue-`, and with a speech engine for one without `+asr-` or without `-n<digits>` and for the
  stubs `recording has no picture; its speech is not read by this version`, `recording's picture cannot be
  decoded on this Mac (VP9 or AV1)` and `no text read on screen; speech is not read by this version`; never for
  the running version or an emitter above it. `_EMITTER_VERSION` is `1.1.0` (the page gained speech, the cue and
  voices) with `_REREAD_BELOW` left at `1.0.0`, so the bump alone reads nothing again. **Pieces:** a picture piece's key is `<piece ticks>|<picture version>|<picture options
  hash>`, without the cue or speech parts, so the picture pieces of a recording stay valid when a speech engine
  appears or fails. S8 is one more piece, numbered past the picture pieces, keyed `speech|<media identity>|<speech
  identity>|<hash of the speech_lines options and the diarizer threshold>` (the media helper decodes the sound), holding the whole file's words (hole repair spliced), segments,
  silent runs, unrecognised gaps and decoded length; `audio.pcm` is decoded into the scratch folder, never kept
  and never a key. It is charged to the allowance like a piece, stops before it when the allowance is used up
  and this call read a piece, and has its own deadline, `60 + 0.07 x seconds of sound` (`_SPEECH_S`, from the
  container's length); past it `RecordingNotFinished(timed_out=True)` with `done_ms` the last picture piece's
  start (0 on a speech-only page). After the load, words, segments and gaps starting at or after `read_ms` are
  dropped and silence is cut at the earlier of `read_ms` and the decoded length. **Cue (S7)**, in the last pass
  when `cue.has_cue(profile)`: the `strip` and `label` rows of each read candidate are its `cue.Label`s,
  `cue.requests` over every tick read, `MediaEngine.pills` in chunks of 1,000 ticks, `lit_sets` and `speaking`
  (ticks to ms); the last pass's deadline gains `_TICK_S x ticks`; a `pills` failure is a MediaError (S2).
  **Naming (S8b):** `naming.name_voices` over each voice's merged spans and the lit sets (empty without a cue or
  picture), `vetoed` per `SAID` line of a voice. **Stubs:** with a speech engine and sound, a file with no
  picture or a VP9 / AV1 picture is a speech-only page (`picture_unread` the stub wording above, profile
  `generic`, no states, rows or keyframes); with no speech line it stays a stub (`recording's picture cannot be
  decoded ...` for VP9 / AV1, else the next wording). A page with no printed row is the stub `no text read on
  screen and no speech in the recording` with a speech engine (the P1 wording without one) only when it has no
  speech line either. `no_speech` is `the recording has no sound` with a speech engine and no sound track, else
  None. **Failure:** `Registry.without_speech` is the same registry built without the speech engine (None for
  a registry without one); `convert_file` routes a `SpeechError` there before the OcrError branch, so the page
  keeps its screens and is cached under a version without `+asr-`, which `outdated` reads again.
- `agentsync.convert.recording_page.render` prints them (spec 3.3 to 3.5, S9). Windows: `SPEAKING: <label>` at
  its tick's even second, `SAID vN: <text>` once, at its first word floored to the second, in the state on screen
  then (the states tile `[0, read end)`: the first from 00:00:00, each to the next one's start), the veto `NOTE`
  after its line, `speech detected, no words recognised until HH:MM:SS` at each unrecognised gap and `no sound
  from here to the end of the recording` at `sound_ends_ms`; at one time `SPEAKING` (rank 4), `SAID` (5), `NOTE`
  (6). Speech and labels are cleaned as picture text is. A speech-only page (`picture_unread` set) has no
  heading: each window is its title, then its lines; the index's Facts carry `picture not read: the recording
  has no picture track` when `picture_unread` holds "no picture", else `picture not read: <picture_unread>; an
  H.264 copy reads it (for example yt-dlp -S vcodec:h264)`. Index: What ran rows `speaker cue` (`cue_identity`,
  SPEAKING lines printed; `not run` when `speaking` is None), `speech` and `voices` (`speech.identity`, SAID lines
  printed / voices; `not run` when `speech` is None), each `none found` at 0; a Voices block after Names read on
  screen when a voice was found (table, blank line, one `VOICE` line per voice at its first word in voice order,
  the margin-band `NOTE` after a held-back voice, the gate `NOTE` once at 00:00:00); Gaps and bounds opens with
  `sound ends at`, the 20 longest quiet stretches in time order with `showing a of b`, and `speech not read:
  <no_speech>`. Summaries: the index's `speech not read` becomes `N speech lines, k voices`, and a window's gains
  `, N speech lines`, when speech ran.

**Tests.** `tests/test_speech.py`, `tests/test_speech_lines.py`, `tests/test_cue.py`, `tests/test_voice_naming.py`
(the S8b rules, the FluidAudio floor, no voice vector), `tests/test_convert_recording.py` (the wiring, the
speech-only pages, `test_speech_is_deterministic_on_a_fixed_wav`), `tests/test_recording_page.py`,
`tests/test_recording_grammar.py`, `tests/test_convert_formats.py` (the `.vtt` fixture), `tests/test_media.py`
(`pills` and `audio`, with the real helper where developer tools exist), `tests/test_convert_file.py` (a speech
failure keeps the screens), `tests/test_cycle.py` (a speech engine that appears reopens the record; a `.vtt` page
of `text-plain` is read again once), `tests/test_ops_doctor.py`, `tests/test_install_oneshot.py`.

### 16.36 Fixes from the third bring-back (2026-10-08)

The corporate Mac ran setup prompt v9 at `c7bfdb8` and finished with no stop. Triage:
`docs/research/corporate-bring-back-2026-10-08.md`. This section holds what that round built. None adds a
command, flag, installer option, config key or environment variable. The prompt's text changed, so it is v10.

#### Scope change on a complete pass: only what left scope is retired (amends §9 step 7, §16.12, §16.23)

A local or inbox source whose scope fingerprint changed carries meta `scope_change:<id>` until its first complete
FULL pass. Before this change that pass retired every deletion candidate as `retired:scope-change`, ahead of the
breaker and the two-pass rule. On a source that had never completed a pass, the `exclude` line the loop itself
advises for empty cloud folders therefore released every held deletion at once. Now each candidate is judged: it
is retired `retired:scope-change` (`# [RETIRED]`, breaker-exempt, no purge, the usual alarm line) only if its
path fails the arm's `in_scope` or its `last_seen_run` is before the run recorded in `scope_root:<id>` (a row last
listed under an earlier `path`). Every other candidate is an ordinary absence: the breaker, then the two-pass
rule, then the purge. The absent files still in scope are judged against the live count the pass started with,
minus the retired rows, so files first seen in that pass do not raise the limit, and the source's
`breaker_tripped` reports that judgment: a plain exclude of a large folder neither trips nor reports the breaker.
The flag clears on that pass as before. With `accept-deletions` the breaker is not judged, as before.

Not changed: Graph kinds. After a fingerprint change a drive source still retires every file its complete listing
lacks, in scope or not. Incomplete passes (§16.23) are unchanged.

Known limit: a row last listed before the run recorded in `scope_root` is retired without the breaker or the
two-pass check. That is every row not listed again after `path` moves (by design), and, with `path` unchanged,
the rows absent since before the first run that recorded the root when that run also changed the fingerprint: an
upgrade straight from a build whose fingerprint lacked the always-on excludes, or a config edit in the first run
on a build that records the root.

Tests: `tests/test_cycle.py` (`test_an_exclude_added_while_files_are_absent_retires_only_what_it_excludes`,
`test_an_exclude_with_no_other_absence_retires_its_files_past_the_breaker`,
`test_a_drive_scope_change_still_retires_every_file_its_full_listing_lacks`, the breaker limit with files new in
the pass, and an exclude that covers no mirrored file).

#### A `no converter` stub that stands is not published again

An online-only file that no converter claims was published again in every pass: its row is pending work while it
is online-only with no content hash. When the row already has the very page the refusal would plan (same path,
same page hash, page intact on disk), `_process` sets the verdict to REFUSED and writes nothing, so
`outputs.built_run` keeps the run that first built it and the pass makes no commit for it. The row is pending
work again in each pass while it is online-only with no content hash. Test:
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_the_stub_of_an_online_only_file_nothing_converts_is_published_once`.

#### Purge: the dry run's note and the queue file (`agentsync.governance`)

A dry run of an entry that targets nothing (no blob, no docs path, no item) says nothing is targeted and no
commit would be rewritten; every other dry run says "up to N commit(s)". `run_purge_queue` writes the queue file
after every purge that verified, holding the entries kept so far (held, failed, not verified) and those not yet
tried, and once more after the last entry. A run that stops part-way on anything but a `GovernanceError`
therefore leaves no entry whose purge verified; the entry in flight stays in the file, so a rerun tries it again.
A dry run writes nothing. **Amended (2026-10-11, §16.38 "A purge by selector takes the queue entries it did off
the queue"):** after a verified purge, the entries kept so far also drop the ones that purge covered (`_covers`),
so the run's own write does not put them back; an entry this run already reported as `stays queued:` is kept.
Tests: `tests/test_governance.py` (a dry run that names nothing; a queue run that stops part-way).

#### setup-report: what the v9 report could not say (`agentsync.setup_report`)

**Recent errors merges repeats.** Within one log file, over the lines `_LEVEL_RE` kept, lines in a row that read
the same after their leading time are shown once: the first of them, followed by
` (<n> times in a row, the last at <time>)`. The merge runs after `_scrub_item_paths` and before the Redactor, so
lines that differ only in an item's path or quoted name are one entry, and two sources' lines stay apart. A
launcher line between two repeats does not split them, and a line with no leading time is never merged. When
anything merged, the heading adds
` (<n> as logged: lines in a row that read the same here are shown once, with their count and last time)`;
otherwise the heading is unchanged. The field case was one warning per empty folder, 5 a poll, which filled the
40-line window. `RECENT_ERROR_LINES` (40) now bounds entries, not log lines.

**A redacted doctor line keeps no padding.** `ops.doctor.format_results` pads every check name to the longest
real one, and the report replaced the id inside the padded name afterwards, so the spaces left beside a
placeholder gave the id's length. `_redact_lines` collapses the run of spaces before the first ` — ` on every
line that matches `_DOCTOR_TAG_RE`, in the Doctor section and the install.out tail alike; on every such line, not
only a changed one, because the unchanged lines' width gives the longest name's length as well. `--no-redact`
keeps doctor's alignment.

**Residue check.** It also lists a word of any case joined to a placeholder by `-` or `_`, and a generic home
folder standing before a placeholder (`~/<dir>/<folder-N>`) is no hit (amended in place where the check is
described).

**Legend.** `<folder-N>` reads "folder (under ~/Library/CloudStorage, or a configured source's folder)": the class
has always taken a configured project folder outside CloudStorage too.

**Purge queue: one line from the audit trail.** After the lines under the table, when a purge is queued:
`- audit trail since <day> (the oldest queued day): N purge-enqueued, N purge (one per item erased) and N
purge-summary (one per purge that ran) line(s)`. `_purge_audit` reads `governance.audit_path` once (not above
`_AUDIT_READ`, 32 MiB), skips a line that is not JSON, and counts the records whose `at` day is on or after the
oldest valid queued day; with no valid day it counts the whole trail. Counts only: no id, no hash, no source,
and, like the other lines there, no command.

**Media helper.** The OCR part says whether the media helper is ready, off, or why not, from the probe doctor's
`media` check calls (amended in place in the "Bounded." paragraph and the "OCR." bullet).

#### Setup prompt v10 (amends §16.14, §16.22 and §16.29; README, `scripts/install.sh`, `agentsync.setup_report`, `agentsync.ops.doctor`)

v10 rewords three sentences of the prompt and nothing else. `PROMPT_VERSION` and `SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT` are 10
and the issue form's placeholder is `v10`. v10 moves no step, so it has no entry in `PROMPT_LAYOUTS`. A saved v9
copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy (§16.28).

- **Step 2 names one inbox.** The inbox the prompt names is the folder named inbox beside the docs repo, the one
  `config.ensure_inbox` keeps; it is one of the `kind = "inbox"` sources in `sources.toml`, and any other source
  of that kind is a folder the person added. On a Mac with fourteen such added sources the v9 sentence ("the
  folder of each kind = "inbox" source"), read literally, named fifteen folders as the inbox; the agent announced
  only the one beside the docs repo and logged the wording. Rejected: routing through the line AGENTS.md carries
  (a file read at step 2, and false when the guide lists several folders).
- **The same rule outside the prompt.** README.md and docs/deploy/README.md name the drop folder the same way and
  no longer say a sync keeps it (`ensure_inbox` runs for init and add-source only). doctor's ok line for an empty
  inbox source outside CloudStorage adds "(drop files you save by hand here)" only when the source's path is that
  folder; any other reads "`<root>` is empty", still ok. `status`'s `inbox on|missing|off` part is unchanged: it
  is about every live inbox source. (**Amended 2026-10-11, §16.39 N22:** it is now about the kept inbox.)
- **Step 3 names the two stops with no report.** "Two cases have no report: while you wait for my folder answer
  in step 1, and when step 1 stops because this prompt is not the installer's. Every other stop still ends with
  the report." Step 1's rule stays word for word. The second case is step 1's whole version stop (the `--version`
  line does not end with the prompt's number, or the command says the pasted prompt is not the installer's):
  there the installer says "run no other step of that prompt", and a report of that attempt would replace the
  last real session's. The first build named only the folder wait, which left that stop with two orders (the v10
  rehearsal, 2026-10-08). The report still follows every other stop (no Xcode tools, a git failure): those are
  failures, and their reports matter most. Rejected: a Rules sentence "where a step says to stop, run nothing
  after it", which switches the report off at those two stops as well. **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.61 F25:** since
  v14 step 3 names three cases; the third, a missing checkout, was a parenthesis before the two-case sentence,
  which then required a report at that stop too.
  **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.67 G25:** since v15 the report comes "even after a failure (except in the three cases
  below)", not "always", and the list reads "Three cases have no report and no "## Not used" section" (§16.67
  G5).
- **The report of a stopped copy invites no bring-back** (`scripts/install.sh` `on_exit`; amends §16.28 and
  §16.30). An older copy's own text still runs `--report-only` after `--log-start` stopped it. When
  `friction_attempt_stopped` holds, the test that already picks that run's `NEXT:` ("do not bring it back"), the
  run calls no `write_bring_back` and prints no `bring back:` and no issue link line: an existing `bring-back.md`
  keeps its bytes, the one of the last real session. It printed both lines above that `NEXT:` and wrote the file
  over the good one (the v10 rehearsal). `setup-report.md` is still written, and an install run in such an
  attempt is unchanged.
- **The exclude line names the table and the file as they are** (`arm_local.exclude_advice`, `loop.next_step`;
  amends §16.22). The wait for empty cloud folders ends `in [[source]] id = "<id>" in
  ~/agent-context/sources.toml`: the id in double quotes, as `config.local_source_table` writes it, and the
  config file's path as `loop._shown` writes it (`~/...` under the home folder, else in full). It said
  `id = '<id>' in sources.toml`: a search for the printed text found nothing in the file, and the file's folder
  was not given (the v10 rehearsal). `exclude_advice` takes that path as its third argument. In the
  setup report's Loop line the file is `sources.toml` whatever its path (§16.32, `setup_report._eval_by_name`). The
  `exclude = [...]` value is unchanged and is valid TOML as pasted. doctor's fixes for a source's path or
  sentinel still write `id = '<id>'`: they name no line to search for. **Amended 2026-10-11, §16.39 N19:**
  reversed; each of them names its table by that line only, and now writes `id = "<id>"`.
- **The Not used list glosses hold**: "hold (a legal or records hold, not a pause)".
- Not changed: the fix-request heading's time carries no zone (§16.30: it marks one session, and nothing parses
  it).

### 16.37 The v10 rehearsal's leftovers (2026-10-08, wave B11)

Two rehearsals of setup prompt v10 in sandbox homes (before and after `69694db` landed) left small findings that
need no prompt text. Each was checked by a verifier and a skeptic; where the skeptic corrected the verifier, its
version is the one built. The prompt is still v10. None adds a command, flag, installer option, config key or
environment variable. Plan: `docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md` section B11.

#### setup-report (`agentsync.setup_report`)

- **A report long after the last attempt says nothing was started since** (amends §16.22). When the friction
  log's last attempt has its `end | finished` line, that line is more than `_NEW_SESSION_GAP` (10 minutes) older
  than the report, and install.log has no run that started after it, the Summary adds, after the prompt line:
  `- note: no attempt was started and no install.sh run began since attempt <N> finished at <end>, more than 10
  minutes before this report, so this report is of attempt <N>. A later session whose step 1 command stopped
  before `install.sh --log-start` (no Xcode tools, a git failure) and logged nothing is not in it.`
  **Amended (2026-10-11, §16.40 "The 'nothing started since' note says install.log"):** the note now says
  "install.log has no run that began since attempt <N> finished" where it said "no install.sh run began", and
  adds "(install.log does not log `install.sh --report-only`)" after "before this report"; the condition is
  unchanged. The prompt's
  Xcode and git stops have said "and stop" since v7 and order no line, and step 3 ends every such stop with the
  report, which judged the attempt that had finished before it and said nothing else. The report cannot tell
  such a session from a report written again by hand (its own evidence line asks for one on an idle Mac), so it
  says what it read and claims neither. The outcome, the issue link, `bring-back.md` and the installer's output
  are unchanged. Rejected: `install.sh --report-only` logging a step 1 error for such a session. A report
  written again by hand would then read "failed at step 1", an installer line would count as agent friction, the
  false line would stay in the append-only log, and the local-work patch an earlier report sent would be sent
  again (§16.30). Held for the next prompt revision: the Xcode and git stops log their error before the report.
  **Amended (2026-10-11, §16.43):** built in setup prompt v11.
- **A session that stopped before `--log-start` was asked nothing** (amends §16.22 and §16.32). A header-less
  attempt with no install.sh run counts no folder question and no click beyond the announced ones (`human turns:
  0 (0 questions; 0 clicks; ...)`), and its expected-turns line is `- expected turns: none (step 1's command
  stopped before install.sh --log-start, before the folder list: no folder question and no Allow click)`. The
  stopped-copy line is unchanged.
- **The Loop line lists every wait** (amends K16b and §16.30): `[; WAITING ON YOU: <the wait the loop stopped
  on>[; WAITING ON YOU: <each other wait, in the loop's order>]]`. `(+N more)` is gone: the report's reader
  cannot run `agentsync status`, and doctor's `(yours: see WAITING ON YOU)` pointed at a wait the line hid. The
  waits are few (8 global kinds, plus a breaker wait and 2 empty-folder waits per source), and an exclude list
  still shows as `<path>`.
- **The folder question is "not logged as a question"**: `expected turns:` reads `the folder question (step 1;
  not logged as a question)`, since an unanswered folder question has been logged as a deviation since v7
  (`f82083b`). The re-run and Allow-click texts keep "not logged".
- **The first-sync count says when it was read**: the clause ends `N of M source(s) listed completely (status:
  baseline complete) at least once by the time this report was written`. A scope change clears the baseline and
  a later incomplete listing does not, so the count can be lower than what the first sync saw, and it never
  claims a listing complete now. The pinned words are only appended to. **Amended (2026-10-11, §16.40 "The
  first-sync count names the field it counts"):** reworded; "only appended to" no longer holds.

Not changed, by design: `unexpected N` (§16.36 left it; a group keyed on doctor's check name would call a
stopped background sync the person's, since `heartbeat.<id>` warns the same way for a stale heartbeat), `in
_eval` on the Loop line (the Configuration part names the docs repo), the order of `<folder-N>` numbers (the
order of registration), and the stopped copy's `setup-report.md` (an old copy's own finish line names it).
**Amended 2026-10-11, §16.39 N16:** `unexpected N` now has a `yours N` group beside it, keyed on the loop's
waits and on the incomplete-listing detail, which a stale heartbeat never has.
**Amended (2026-10-11, §16.40 "The Summary names the draft baseline's folder in words"):** the Loop line no
longer reads `in _eval`. `_eval_by_name` writes `in the docs repo's _eval folder` (`_EVAL_SHOWN`); the line
still holds no path, and the live `agentsync status` wait keeps the full path.

#### Installer (`scripts/install.sh`)

- **The helper builds have a step of their own.** The OCR, media and speech helper builds are the install.log
  step `helpers`, right after `launcher`: `result=done` when the modules ran, `skipped note=no-devtools` without
  developer tools, `skipped note=no-interpreter` without the tool's interpreter. Its rc is 0 unless a signal
  stops the run during it, so the exit status is unchanged, and `launcher` times the launcher alone. The speech
  helper's first build took about 100 s in the rehearsal, logged on a `launcher` line that said `skipped
  note=not-requested`. The report reads step names generically, so an older log parses as before.
- **The helper builds print a progress line.** A ticker beside each build prints `helpers: building the
  <OCR|media|speech> helper, still running, <N>s` every `PROGRESS_EVERY` seconds; it is killed after that
  build and in `on_exit` (see the last part of this section). The builds stay in the foreground, so a signal
  to the installer's own pid lets the build under way finish before the run exits, and the re-run its `NEXT:`
  names never meets a second build in the same SwiftPM tree (a backgrounded build was measured to outlive the
  installer) (**amended 2026-10-11, B13 (§16.41):** a stop of the whole process group, even SIGKILL, stops the
  build tool and its compilers within seconds, so that re-run does not meet one either).

#### Sync and status around deletions and re-reads (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.manifest`)

- Between the pass that marks a file absent and the pass that removes it, `status` ends that source's line with
  `· absent N (turned into deletion notices by a later complete pass if still missing)`, from `Manifest.absent_counts()` (present,
  non-directory rows carrying `extra.absent_since_run`), unless the source's deletion breaker is tripped: then
  nothing is removed until `accept-deletions`, and the breaker field already counts the held files. The count
  stays out of `SourceStatus`, which feeds the committed `_sync/STATE.snapshot.md`.
- The pass that removes a local or inbox file still absent from a second complete pass adds the alarm `N file(s)
  still absent from this complete pass: their pages are now deletion notices (deleted upstream; purge queued)`.
  Graph sources and `accept-deletions` are unchanged. **Amended 2026-10-11, §16.39 H23:** unchanged in the alarm
  (they raise none); the line of their source now says `K turned into deletion notices (deleted upstream)`, as the
  line of this pass does.
  **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.51 Q16:** the status suffix reads `· absent N (each becomes a deletion notice on a
  later complete pass if still missing)` and the sync line `K page(s) turned into deletion notice(s) (deleted
  upstream)`; the alarms are unchanged.
  **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R105:** the three literals above and the marking pass's alarm (`N file(s) absent from this complete pass:
  their pages become deletion notices only if still absent next pass`) said "removed"; the page stays in the
  mirror as a `[DELETED UPSTREAM]` stub until `tombstone_reap_days`, so they now say "deletion notices", plural
  because an `.eml` tombstones its attachment pages with it. `; purge queued` is printed only when
  `purge_on_upstream_delete` is on (the default; `archive = true` turns it off).
- When the sync header's `0 change(s)` (it counts `MirrorChange` rows) sits beside a commit, it adds ` (no
  source changed a mirror page; the commit holds other docs-repo files)`: a baseline flip in INDEX.md and the
  snapshot, or the agent's `_eval` drafts. Marking a file absent never commits.
- `CycleReport.read_again` is the run's re-read tally; the summary line reads `converted N, deferred M
  online-only, read again R` when R > 0, unchanged otherwise. A re-read of the same bytes is never in N
  (§16.27); a file whose bytes changed under its re-read counts in both.

#### The alarm of a source whose unknown folders are all empty cloud folders (`agentsync.arm_local`)

When every unknown folder of a `kind = "local"` walk is a zero-child cloud folder below the root, the alarm
reads `N unknown dir(s) — empty cloud folder(s), zero children in a cloud tree: ...; enumeration incomplete, no
deletions this pass (see the WAITING ON YOU line about <id>, which agentsync status also prints)`. It offered
Files and Folders access and an exclude above a wait that names the cause, and that can warn against an exclude
(a folder that held mirrored files). Any other unknown folder and any inbox keep the old text, which is then the
only line naming the other causes.
**Amended 2026-10-11, §16.39 N27:** the pointer now reads `(each WAITING ON YOU line about <id> says what to
do, and agentsync status prints them)`, for an inbox as for a local source. When an unreadable folder sits beside
an empty cloud folder, the alarm keeps the old cause and ends `(grant the agent Files and Folders access for the
other folders; for the empty ones, each WAITING ON YOU line about <id> says what to do, and agentsync status
prints them)`. Only a walk with no empty cloud folder below the root keeps the old text.

#### Purge dry run (`agentsync.governance`)

A dry run's headline names no commit count and says the cache entries "would be removed" (`purge <kind>
(<reason>): dry run · N item(s) · N docs path(s) · N blob(s) targeted · N cache entr(ies) would be removed`);
the note below it carries the commit count (§16.36). A real run's headline is unchanged. **Amended 2026-10-11,
§16.39 N36:** both runs' headlines spell the cache count out, `N cache entries` (`1 cache entry` for one), and
neither says `entr(ies)`.

Tests: `tests/test_setup_report.py`, `tests/test_install_oneshot.py`, `tests/test_launcher.py`,
`tests/test_cli.py` (status, the sync header and summary, the purge dry run), `tests/test_cycle.py` and
`tests/test_arm_local.py`.

#### The first sync's read-again count reaches the report (`scripts/install.sh`, `agentsync.setup_report`)

The installer logs its first-sync note as `converted-N-deferred-M-reread-R` when the sync's line ends `, read
again R` (R > 0), and as `converted-N-deferred-M` otherwise, so an older install.log and R = 0 parse as before.
The Summary's first-sync clause reads `converted N, deferred M online-only, read again R (<source>...)` when the
note, or with no note the sync's own line in install.out, carries R. Why: the second v10 rehearsal's installer
printed `read again 2` and the report's clause dropped it. **Amended (2026-10-11, §16.40 "The first-sync line
counts what other runs read again"):** the clause also counts, after `· since this install run began, `, what runs
other than the installer's sync read again; the installer's own `read again R` is unchanged.

#### The helpers ticker names the helper it waits for (`scripts/install.sh`)

The ticker runs beside each build, not beside all three, and prints `helpers: building the <OCR|media|speech>
helper, still running, <N>s`, its seconds counted from that build's start; it is killed after the build,
before the helper's line, and in `on_exit`. The builds stay in the foreground and a line still comes at least
every 15 s. Why: both v10 rehearsals printed 12 and 13 `helpers: still running` lines (about 3 minutes) after
the OCR and media lines said ready, then `speech: off (the speech models are not placed: ...)`; the time was
the speech helper's first build, and nothing said so. The speech line is the module's probe and is unchanged,
still one line: no tick starts with `speech:`.

### 16.38 Purge: a live file keeps what it holds (2026-10-11, wave B13 lane A)

#### A purge keeps another file's live page at a purged path, and its rows (amends §16.7, §16.12)

A targeted docs path where a worktree HEAD holds a blob the purge did not target is *taken*: another file's live
page sits where the purged item's page once was (an upstream deletion's tombstone was reaped and a new file, often
with the same name, was published to the freed path before the queue ran). The outputs, tombstones and depends
rows keyed by that path stay, the history's index files keep the lines that name it by path, and the live item's
own `_manifest` line stays by its id even when it names the same source path. Logs, run errors and ignored files
are still scrubbed by it. The manifest re-read runs inside pass 1's fixpoint, so pass 1 walks with the page paths
pass 2 treats as explicit; a path is taken only where pass 2 keeps the blob, and the preview's blob and item
counts are the real run's. `PurgeReport` gains `taken_paths: tuple[str, ...] = ()`, set in the dry run too;
`agentsync purge` prints `  taken: <path> (another file's live page is there now: its manifest row and index
lines stay)` after the `path:` lines. `verified` is unchanged. Why: the purge deleted the live file's outputs row,
depends rows, manifest line and DEPENDS.tsv line while it reported VERIFIED, and a repair pass then deleted the
live page as an orphan. Residuals: lines in history that name only the taken path (a CHANGELOG `- A`/`- D` line,
an older DEPENDS.tsv row) stay, which leaks nothing new because the path is the live page's own name in HEAD; a
live item with an outputs row at the path but no page there in HEAD still loses its row. Tests:
`tests/test_governance.py::test_purge_keeps_the_rows_and_index_lines_of_another_item_now_at_the_purged_path`,
`::test_purge_keeps_the_manifest_line_of_a_new_file_with_the_same_name`,
`::test_purge_marks_no_path_taken_that_the_rewrite_drops`.

#### `purge --queue` keeps an upstream deletion of a file that is listed again (`agentsync.governance`, `agentsync.setup_report`; done from §16.30 "Not done here")

`run_purge_queue` asks `_kept_upstream_deletion` before each entry. For reason `upstream-deleted` only, the rows a
purge of the entry would delete (`_resolve_manifest`: its own id, an alias followed to the current id) are read;
one in state `live` or `dataless` keeps the entry queued with a `PurgeReport` that is not verified (`not_run`, new
field, "" when the entry ran; `remote` "not run"; the note ``stays queued: the manifest lists the file as live or
online-only (N row(s)[, K of them under a later id]); an upstream deletion is not run against a listed file; a
later `purge --queue` runs it once the file is gone``; **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.50 Q45:** was `..., and runs
once the file is gone again`, which read as a run nobody starts), in a dry run too. The note names no id and no
path. `quarantined` and
`refused` rows still run: after a file comes back refused, the queued purge is the only erasure of its earlier
text. `label-escalation`, `dlp-remediation`, `erasure-request` and `operator` entries are never judged. A kept
entry exits 1 as a held one does and writes no audit line; `purge --queue`'s last line counts only the entries
that ran (`N queued purge(s) run; M still queued`). The report's `still listed` line under the purge table says
whether a run keeps those entries queued, keeps some and erases the others (with both counts), or would erase
them all.

The same-path rule in `_Rewriter` skips an id the manifest lists (any state but tombstone, or an alias of such a
row; `_ManifestTargets.others`, passed to both passes): that is another file's earlier page, not the purged
item's before an unrecorded re-key. A `.files` dir at an explicit page path is dropped only in a tree whose page
there is targeted or absent. Why: the 2026-10-07 field queue held upstream deletions of files that were back, and
a rename followed by a new file under the old name let a purge of the new file erase the renamed live file, its
page in HEAD and its history while it reported VERIFIED. Tests: `tests/test_governance.py::
test_purge_queue_runs_an_upstream_deletion_of_a_file_that_came_back_refused`,
`::test_purge_spares_a_live_file_whose_earlier_page_path_a_deleted_file_took`,
`::test_purge_queue_keeps_an_upstream_deletion_of_a_file_that_is_listed_again`, the `still listed` pins in
`tests/test_setup_report.py`, and `tests/test_cli.py::test_purge_queue_keeps_an_upstream_deletion_of_a_live_file_and_does_not_count_it_as_run`.

#### A purge by selector takes the queue entries it did off the queue (`agentsync.governance`; amends §16.36 "Purge: the dry run's note and the queue file")

A verified `purge()` (never a dry run) takes off `purge-queue.json`, under the same writer lock, every queued
entry it covers (`_covers`): the entry names one item by source and stable id, the purge erased that id (or it as
an alias: `report.items` holds the item's retired ids), the purge was not narrowed by `--source` to another
source (a docs glob can match another source's page and erases only that page), and the purge suppressed the item
if the entry's purge would have: an `upstream-deleted` purge suppresses nothing, so it leaves a queued
`label-escalation`, `dlp-remediation`, `erasure-request` or `operator` entry of the same item. A queue file this
build cannot read or write is logged and left byte-for-byte as it was; the purge still returns its verified
report. After a verified purge, `run_purge_queue`'s entries kept so far also drop the ones that purge covered, so
its own write does not put them back; an entry this run already reported as `stays queued:` is not dropped (its
report stands, and the next run clears it once the file is gone). Why: the v10 bring-back's `agentsync purge id=...` erased an item and left
its queued purge waiting in every wait line. Tests: `tests/test_governance.py::
test_a_purge_by_selector_takes_the_queued_purges_it_did_off_the_queue`,
`::test_a_purge_leaves_a_queued_purge_it_cannot_stand_in_for`.

#### The purge wait names the preview before the run (`agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.cycle`; amends §16.20 and §16.30)

Every text that asks the operator to run the purge queue names the preview first (BIN below is the installed
`~/.local/bin/agentsync`; STATE.md, the alarm and doctor's fix write `agentsync`):

- the loop's wait: ``N queued purge(s): preview with `BIN purge --queue --dry-run` (writes nothing) before you
  run `BIN purge --queue` (rewrites history)``
- `status`: ``queued purges: N (preview with `BIN purge --queue --dry-run` before `BIN purge --queue`)``
- doctor's `governance.purge_queue` fix: `agentsync purge --queue --dry-run (a preview that writes nothing); then
  agentsync purge --queue`, in the house fix grammar (a command, a parenthesis, then prose after `;`)
- STATE.md's queued-purges line: ``- N purge request(s) waiting; preview with `agentsync purge --queue
  --dry-run`, then run `agentsync purge --queue` (rewrites history)``
- the label-escalation alarm ends with `cycle._PURGE_QUEUE_STEPS`, ``(preview with `agentsync purge --queue
  --dry-run` before `agentsync purge --queue`)``, which any later alarm that queues a purge uses too.
- **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R46/R47/R57:** the credential rescan's alarm (§16.39 N5, ``a published page
  matches the secret scan's new rules: ...``) ended ``(run `agentsync purge --queue`)`` with no preview; it now
  ends with `cycle._PURGE_QUEUE_STEPS` too (`tests/test_credential_rescreen.py`, the two tests that read it).

Each text keeps its head (`N queued purge(s): `, `queued
purges: N (`, `- N purge request(s) waiting; `, `label escalation:`), so readers keyed on the prefix are unchanged.
Why: a run rewrites history and cannot be undone (with `--push`, the remote too); the wait knows only the count,
while the preview prints each entry's reason and docs paths, and which entries the run keeps queued. Tests:
`tests/test_loop.py::test_the_purge_wait_names_the_preview_before_the_run` and the pins it moved in
`tests/test_loop.py`, `tests/test_cli.py`, `tests/test_setup_report.py`, `tests/test_e2e.py` and
`tests/test_review_fixes.py::test_sg04`.

#### accept-deletions on an incomplete pass keeps the breaker (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.loop`)

`accept-deletions SOURCE` (and `reconcile --accept-deletions`) applies no deletion and keeps the source's deletion
breaker when its pass leaves a known file unlisted (`Manifest.unseen_live`, less the rows retired this pass on the
config's word): an incomplete listing proves no absence. Its source line then reads `BREAKER TRIPPED` while the
breaker is active, and it adds the alarm `accept-deletions applied no deletion: this pass did not list the whole source,
so no absent file is confirmed; the deletion breaker still holds N file(s): once a sync lists SOURCE in full, run
`agentsync accept-deletions SOURCE` again`. Without an active breaker (none tripped, or its hold expired) the
alarm is only its first clause. A pass
that lists every known file clears the breaker, complete or not, because the breaker holds no file then (a breaker
whose files came back is cleared only by this verb, so keeping it there would leave a dead wait on a source that
stays incomplete, such as one with an empty cloud folder or a folder with no access). Exit code unchanged (0).
The loop's breaker wait adds ` once a sync lists SOURCE in full` when the source's last full listing was
incomplete; for a complete source it is unchanged. Why: clearing on an incomplete pass spent the operator's
assertion, applied nothing, and the next complete pass tripped again on the same files. The designer's first rule
(clear only on a complete pass) was measured worse than main when nothing is absent, so the built rule keys on
known files left unlisted. Tests: `tests/test_e2e.py::test_f_accept_deletions_on_an_incomplete_pass_keeps_the_breaker`,
`::test_f_accept_deletions_clears_a_breaker_whose_files_came_back_on_an_incomplete_pass`,
`tests/test_loop.py::test_the_breaker_wait_of_an_incomplete_source_asks_for_a_full_listing_first`.

### 16.39 Sync, status and doctor fixes (2026-10-11, wave B13 lane B)

#### N5: credential stubs are screened again when the secret-scan rules change (`agentsync.lints`, `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.manifest`)

`lints.secret_rules_identity()` is `{"rules": sha256(SECRET_RULES_VERSION, the builtin patterns, the Teams
join-link carve-out, the text suffixes), "gitleaks": "<resolved path>:<size>:<mtime_ns>" or ""}`: a stat, never a
gitleaks run. The manifest meta `secret_rules` keeps the one of the last re-screen. When it differs at the start
of a run (an update, gitleaks installed or upgraded, or none stored yet, which is every install's first run on
this build), `_Cycle._check_secret_rules` marks every `contains a credential` stub of a local or inbox source
that is on this Mac as a `[policy]` re-screen marks a file (`Manifest.mark_quarantined_rescreen`: hashes
forgotten, verdict MAYBE_CHANGED), and it is converted and scanned again. An online-only one waits in the meta
`secret_rescreen_waiting` until it is on this Mac, and nothing is downloaded; Graph rows are screened again when
their bytes change. The log line is INFO and carries counts only.

A file that is or ever was a credential stub is screened before anything is written (`_Cycle._still_credential`,
in a private folder under the staging folder; the copy gitleaks reads is made in that folder too, never in the
system's temporary folder), by the builtin patterns as well when gitleaks scans
(`lints.lint_secrets(..., builtin_too=)`): gitleaks replaces the builtin patterns and does not flag a plain
`Password: Welcome123` (measured, gitleaks 8.30.1), so neither a rules change nor gitleaks arriving publishes
what the builtin patterns still match. A hit writes the credential stub: no page and no sidecar, and for a file
that is that stub already no tombstone, CHANGELOG line or commit either; the fresh conversion is deleted from the
cache. This holds for every later conversion of the file (its bytes changed), not only for a re-screen.

Which files those are is the meta `secret_once_credential`, a JSON list of `[source_id, item id]` that
`_Cycle._publish` adds to when it writes a credential stub or meets one, and that a file leaves only when the
manifest forgets it. A safe-save that gives the file a new id moves its entry to that id in the rekey's own
transaction (`_Cycle._rekey_credential`; pinned by
`test_a_stub_saved_under_a_new_file_id_is_still_screened_as_a_stub`); a file that returns under a new id with
no pairing (a copy, a move to another source) is a new file to the record, as it is to the scan. It outlives the row's reason on purpose (fix pass, 2026-10-11): the run that screens a stub
again may not be able to read it (the conversion fails, the OCR helper is missing or its time is used up), and
then writes a `no converter` or `conversion failed` stub, or the page of what it could read once the screen passes
that part. The run that reads the rest is a re-read of a row that no longer says `contains a credential`, and it
is screened the same way all the same. Without the record, gitleaks alone read that text and a password in a
picture was committed (measured on this item's first build, before the record: an image, and a PDF with a
scanned page).

Every published page, its text sidecars and every stub page are scanned again once per move (meta
`secret_rescan_pending`, set with the identity and cleared when a run's secret scan has run; a run that fails
earlier keeps it). A page the scan now matches becomes a credential stub, its cached conversions are deleted and a
`dlp-remediation` purge is queued, with an alarm and a WARNING that name the source id and the opaque item id
only. A stub the scan matches carries the credential in the file's name: its path is redacted, as a first write
under those rules would. The scan reads the pages of every source, also under `sync --source`; a hit
in a source the run did not select raises its alarm in the report and writes that source no heartbeat.

A run without the gitleaks the stored identity names marks nothing, waiting stubs included, and keeps the stored
value: launchd's PATH lacks a gitleaks that only a shell PATH finds, and a scan without it must not decide what
it stubbed. `tests/test_credential_rescreen.py` pins a hash of the code that decides a hit to
`SECRET_RULES_VERSION`: a change that decides differently bumps the version, a comment or docstring edit only
updates the pin.

**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R75:** a run from the shell records the gitleaks its PATH finds
(`lints.remember_gitleaks`, in `agentsync sync` and `agentsync install-agent`), and a LaunchAgent run uses that
one (`lints.gitleaks_lookup` tries `lints.recorded_gitleaks` before PATH and the fixed places, which now include
`/opt/local/bin`, `~/.local/bin` and `~/go/bin`). Both kinds of run read the record first, so the identity does
not move between them; the shell-PATH residual below holds only until the first such run from the shell.

Residuals, none worse than before: a gitleaks found only on a shell PATH, where a marked row is converted in a
later launchd run (byte budget, `sync --source`) or the first run on this build is a launchd run, has that row
judged by the builtin patterns alone, as every changed file on such an install already is; once gitleaks is
removed after a run that had it, nothing is screened again until it is back; `[governance] archive` pages are not
scanned again; the published-page scan uses the scan of the run (gitleaks alone when there is one), as every new
page does.

**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R76:** the "new id is a new file to the scan" and "gitleaks alone when there is
one" residuals are gone. `lints.lint_secrets` runs the builtin patterns over every page it scans, and gitleaks
beside them when there is one (`builtin_too=` is removed: every page is read that way now), so a copy, a move to
another source or a delete-then-recreate of a stubbed file, and any new page with a plain `Password: ...`, is a
credential stub on a Mac with gitleaks too. `generic-password` passes over a bracketed hint, which holds a
space (`(minimum 8 characters)`, `<your password>`) or is one placeholder word (`{password}`, `[redacted]`), and
over a value of mask characters only (`*`, `x`, `.`, `•`, `-`; trailing punctuation allowed); a bracketed value
that is neither (`(Welcome123)`, `<S3cr3t!x>`) and a value after a hint are hits. `SECRET_RULES_VERSION` is 2,
so every install scans its published pages once more under both changes.
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R74:** `[governance] archive` pages are scanned again too (the residual above is
closed). The rescan also reads every `archive/` page whose frontmatter says `status: archived`, with the text
sidecars under its `.files/` folder, symlinks skipped (`_Cycle._add_archive_pages`). They are no output rows and
never become a stub: a hit deletes the copy and its sidecars, rewrites the item's mirror tombstone without the line
naming the copy when that tombstone is still there, deletes the item's cached conversions and queues a
`dlp-remediation` purge named by the copy's own frontmatter ids, with the same alarm head and WARNING
(`_Cycle._archived_credential`). Test:
`test_an_archive_page_the_new_rules_match_is_deleted_and_queues_a_purge`.

Why: the 2026-10-05 join-link fix (de081ae) never reached the invites quarantined before it; nothing stored what
rules a stub was made under. Tests: `tests/test_credential_rescreen.py`.

#### H23: the sync line tells the marking pass from the removing pass (`agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.publish`)

`deletion_candidate=N` on a source's sync line still counts every file absent from a complete full pass: the
classifier counts them before their outcome is known, so the count is the same on the pass that marks a file and
on the pass that removes it. `SourceReport` carries the outcome as two counts, last in the class and 0 by
default: `absent_marked` (a local or inbox file absent for the first time, kept) and `absent_removed` (a file
removed this pass as deleted upstream: a local or inbox file on its second absence, a Graph item or a file under
`accept-deletions` on its first). `_Cycle._confirmed_absent` is the one place that sets them. The source's line
prints `M marked absent` and `K turned into deletion notices (deleted upstream)` (**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R105:** was `K removed
as deleted upstream`), each only when nonzero, after `BREAKER TRIPPED`
and before the cursor's word; a pass with neither prints the line it always did. `_sync/STATE.md`'s `this_run:`
line adds ` · absent_marked: M` and ` · absent_removed: K` after `materialised_bytes`, each only when nonzero.

A tripped breaker and a scope change add to neither: the line says `BREAKER TRIPPED`, the scope-change alarm
says `retired`. So `deletion_candidate` = marked + removed + held by the breaker + retired by a scope change. A
dry run acts on nothing and counts nothing. `counts` and `run_sources.counts_json` are unchanged.

Why: B11's final rehearsal printed the same counter on both passes and only the alarm told them apart; the
removal under `accept-deletions` or on a Graph source raises no alarm (§16.37), so its line said nothing at all.
Tests: `tests/test_cli.py`, `tests/test_e2e.py`, `tests/test_cycle.py`.

#### N23: status counts refused files apart from quarantined ones (`agentsync.publish`, `agentsync.cycle`, `agentsync.cli`)

`SourceStatus` carries `quarantined` (file rows in state quarantined) and `refused` (file rows in state refused)
as two counts; before, `quarantined` was their sum (`cycle.source_statuses`). Every reader prints both:
`agentsync status` prints `quarantined Q · refused R · deferred D` on the source's line, `_sync/STATE.md` prints
`quarantined: Q · refused: R · deferred: D`, and the committed `_sync/STATE.snapshot.md` has a `refused` column
after `quarantined`. The column arrives with the next commit that has content; it makes none of its own, and
nothing reads the snapshot back.

STATE.md's read-side contract names both, because `_sync/QUARANTINE.tsv` lists both: `` `quarantined > 0` or
`refused > 0` → name the counts, point at `_sync/QUARANTINE.tsv`: unreadable, not absent``. With the old line a
source that holds only refused files would read `quarantined: 0` and send no agent to the file.

The two counts are the manifest's file rows by state, as the setup report's Quarantine part counts them. They
are not the sync line's `quarantined=` and `refused=`: those count what one pass stubbed, and a failed
conversion is `error=` on the sync line and a quarantined row here, so status's `quarantined` can be the larger
number even on the pass that wrote the stubs. The
report's Overlapping-sources part still prints their sum as `stubs N` (§16.28). Why: a field report's status
said `quarantined 11` beside a Quarantine part with 0 quarantined and 11 refused. Tests: `tests/test_cli.py`
(the status line), `tests/test_publish.py` (STATE.md, its contract line, the snapshot).

#### N36: the purge headline spells its cache count (`agentsync.cli`)

The cache count in the purge headline reads `1 cache entry` or `N cache entries` (0 included), followed by `would
be removed` on a dry run and `removed` on a real run; it never reads `entr(ies)`. The other counts keep `(s)`
(`item(s)`, `docs path(s)`, `commit(s)`, `blob(s)`), as every other CLI line does. Why: the v10 rehearsal read
`entr(ies)` as a typo. Amends §16.37 "Purge dry run" (dated line there). Tests: `tests/test_cli.py`.

#### N3: a failed re-read under a new version is still left (`agentsync.cycle`)

`_Cycle._reread_source` counted what was left against the targets it took before reading. A re-read the engine
failed on writes this build's version without an engine: a PDF's page without `+ocr-`, or an image's `no
converter` stub. When the file's version before the read differed from that, no target named the new one. The
old version could be an older emitter, the field build, or a pypdfium2 or pdfminer.six the install has since
upgraded. The cycle then stored `done` with the file at one failure, and the file never got the second read
§16.27 gives it. A field-build image kept the stub, without its text, even once the engine worked again.

When the cycle has read a file of the source again (`_reread_n` moved during the call), the count now asks for
the targets again after the reads (`_reread_targets`). So the run record's `reread_left` and the `sync again`
note count that file, the next cycle reads it, and a second failure puts it in `tried`. A call that read
nothing counts against the targets it took, as before. Cost: one more `produced_by` statement for a source in
which the cycle read a file again. Amends §16.27 "The record", `done` (dated line there). Tests:
`tests/test_cycle.py`, a scan from emitter 2.0.0 the engine fails on (read in two cycles, then given up), and a
field-build image the engine fails on once (its text is back in the next cycle).

#### N4: an upgrade restarts the re-read (`agentsync.cycle`)

The build's part of `_Cycle._capabilities` is `cycle._build_digest(_BUILD_ROOT)`: a sha256 over the files of
the installed `agentsync` package (each one's path under the package and the sha256 of its bytes, in path order,
`__pycache__/` and `*.pyc` left out), worked out once a process. It was `__version__`, which has been `0.1.0`
since the first commit: two builds gave the same `for`, a source's record with its `tried` files carried over,
and a file given up under one build was never tried by the next, although §16.27 and the README ("left alone
until it changes or agentsync is upgraded") said it was. The README sentence is unchanged and now true.

Not the install stamp's commit: install.sh writes none for a changed checkout or a wheel, and every commit would
move it. A commit that changes no packaged file restarts nothing; the two deploy docs the wheel carries
(`agentsync/_deploy/`) are packaged files, so an edit to either restarts the scan once, and a checkout run and
the installed tool hash differently (the record's second slot keeps both, so going between them costs a manifest
query, not repeated attempts). A dependency upgrade alone does not move the digest and restarts nothing: `for`
holds each converter's `outdated_key` (its emitter and floor), not its version string, so a file given up stays
given up until a packaged file changes. **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R100:** no longer so: `for` holds the converter libraries'
distribution versions (`deps`, §16.27 "The record"), so a library upgrade alone (a `uv sync` that moves pdfminer.six
or pypdfium2) restarts the scan once, as a new build does, and a file given up under the old library gets its two
attempts under the new one. A file or a folder that cannot be read (a tree an install is replacing
under a running sync) counts as such: the digest is still made, and the next process starts over once more.

The first sync on the build that carries this changes every source's `for` once: each scan runs again (a
manifest query; only files that still lack something are read) and a given-up file gets its two attempts again,
inside the cycle's 120 s re-read budget and the three-in-a-row stop. Every later install that changes a packaged
file does the same, which is what a new engine or floor already did. Amends §16.27 (two dated lines there).
Tests: `tests/test_cycle.py` (the digest follows bytes and names, not mtimes or compiled caches; a folder that
cannot be listed still gives one; two files given up are read again, once, under another build).

#### N11: a doctor fix names a home path as `~/'<rest>'` (`agentsync.ops.doctor`, `agentsync.setup_report`)

The rule covers the eleven places where a doctor fix wrote a path in single quotes: the state folder's
`mkdir`, "move ... aside", `chown` and `chmod 700`, the `chmod 600` of its files, a source folder's
`chmod u+rx`, the `--canary` argument, the plist in `launchctl bootstrap`, the log truncation, and the
`docs_repo.permissions` `chmod` and `git -C`. There a path below the home folder is written `~/'<rest>'` (`ops.doctor._shell_path`; the home folder itself is `~`), and any other path stays
`'<path>'`. The home folder is the one `HOME` gives or the one it resolves to, the two forms the setup report
registers; a home folder that does not resolve (a symlink loop) is taken as spelled. The quoted part is the raw
path, so the report's redaction finds every name in it as before, and these fixes no longer carry the login
name. A path that holds `'` breaks the quoting, as it did before.

Every other path in doctor's output is as it was, absolute and unquoted, and a report still redacts its home
folder to `~`: the detail of every check, and the fixes that wrote a path without quotes. Those are the
config file to delete, the docs repo in `mkdir -p`, "move ... aside", `git -C ... rm --cached` and "the real
directory", the folder to open in Finder, the sentinel to restore, the volume to free space on, the log folder
to read a crash in, the launcher path that begins the canary command, and the Full Disk Access fix, whose
path is pasted into Finder. Most of them are prose, not a command; the docs repo's `mkdir -p` and `git -C`
copied from a report run with `~` expanded and break only on a space in the path, as before.

Why: both setup reports redact the home folder to `~`, and no shell expands a tilde inside quotes. The
`docs_repo.permissions` fix copied from a report failed with `chmod: ~/agent-context: No such file or directory`
(field report 2026-10-06, row 9). Measured in the design: the state folder's mode fix failed the same way, and
its `mkdir -m 700 -p '~/...'` exited 0 having made a folder named `~` in the working directory.
`setup_report.residue()`'s home-container rule accepts the quote after `~/`, so `~/'Development/<folder-1>'` is
no residue hit. Amends §16.29 "A re-run does not stop on a permission agentsync clears itself" (dated line
there). Tests: `tests/test_ops_doctor.py` (the state-folder and permissions fixes run under `/bin/sh` as the
report shows them; the forms), `tests/test_setup_report.py` (the residue rule).

#### N19: doctor's source fixes name the table as sources.toml writes it (`agentsync.ops.doctor`)

The five fixes that name a `[[source]]` table by its id line write `[[source]] id = "<id>"`, as
`config.local_source_table`, `config.inbox_source_table` and `graph.discover._toml_str` write that line:

- no path configured (`source.<id>`);
- a missing path (`source.<id>.listable` and `source.<id>.volume`);
- a path that is not a folder (`source.<id>.listable`);
- a missing sentinel (`source.<id>.sentinel`);
- the launcher's canary reports the folder missing (`tcc.<id>`).

The wording is otherwise unchanged. An id matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, so nothing in it needs escaping.

Why: they wrote Python's `id = '<id>'`. A search of sources.toml for the printed text found nothing, and the
setup prompt's single-quoted `--log` FIX argument had to rewrite the quote. §16.36 fixed the same for the
exclude line and left these, on the reason that they name no line to search for; they name their table by
that line only. Residual: a sources.toml written by hand with a TOML literal string (`id = 'x'`) no longer
matches the printed text; agentsync writes no such line and no doc shows one. Amends §16.32 (the volume row
and the listable fix, in place: both state the text a check prints) and §16.36 (dated line there). Tests:
`tests/test_ops_doctor.py` (`test_a_source_fix_names_the_table_as_sources_toml_writes_it`, two expectations).

#### N30: the permission sample is not spent in trees walked on their own (`agentsync.ops.doctor`)

`docs_repo.permissions` walks each folder it checks (the docs repo, its `.git/objects`, its `mirror/`, the
cache, the logs) and looks at up to 500 entries below each (`_PERM_SAMPLE`). The walk of one of those folders
no longer counts or enters another of them that lies inside it (`_group_other_readable(root, own_roots)`): the
docs repo's walk leaves out `.git/objects` and `mirror/`, and a log folder configured inside the docs repo (a
cache folder there is refused when the config is read); a cache or log folder configured above the docs repo
leaves the docs repo out. Each is still walked as a root of its own, with its own 500 entries, and that walk
checks the folder's own mode. The context folder (the one that holds sources.toml and the docs repo) is not
one of them: only its own mode is read, so a walk that holds it enters it, and a cache or log folder
configured above it still reports a loose file beside the docs repo. The rest of `.git` (index, refs, logs, config, hooks) stays in the docs repo's walk, because no
other root covers it; the test pins that. A root spelled through a symlink or with `..` matches no path the
walk yields and is walked twice, as before.

Why: the docs repo's walk spent its 500 entries inside `.git/objects` (490 entries for 300 committed pages,
measured) and `mirror/`, so an agent's folder the file system lists after them was never looked at and status
said `[ok]` over a file group and other could read (triage 2026-10-06). A file system lists a folder in an
order of its own, so which folders were hidden differed by file system. A loose page in `mirror/` is now
reported once, not twice, so `(+N more)` counts paths. In a large repo a loose folder outside `_eval/` and
`topics/` now FAILs with the chmod, as it already did in a small one; those two trees are made owner-only by
every sync and by the config step, within the reach §16.29 states. Amends §16.12 (dated line there). Tests:
`tests/test_cycle.py` (`test_the_permissions_sample_is_not_spent_in_trees_walked_on_their_own`,
`test_a_cache_folder_above_the_context_folder_does_not_hide_what_is_in_it`).

#### N16: the Summary's doctor line names the person's own waits (`agentsync.setup_report`, `agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.cli`)

Between `expected N: ...` and `unexpected N`, the Summary's doctor line has a third group, printed only when it
is not empty: `yours N: <check names> (see WAITING ON YOU)`. `NextStep` gains `checks: tuple[str, ...] = ()`.
`loop.next_step` adds `governance.purge_queue` when it writes the queued-purge wait, and `heartbeat.<id>` when
it writes a wait for a local source whose listing stops at a held privacy prompt, at an empty cloud folder, or
at a folder it cannot list. It adds no other check, and `NextStep.lines()` is unchanged, so sync, status and
STATE.md print what they printed.

The CLI's `ReportHooks.loop_next` returns that `NextStep`, or `[]` when the loop state cannot be read. The Loop
line reads its lines as before, and a hook that returns lines is still accepted.

A doctor warn is "yours" when its check name is in those `checks` and, for a `heartbeat.<id>` warn, its detail
starts `enumeration incomplete for `. That check also warns for no successful pass and for a last success
older than 3 x cadence. No wait explains those, and a background sync that stopped gives them too, so they stay
"unexpected" even while the source's wait is listed.

The group never reads doctor's notes or fixes, so a report run by hand and one written under install.sh put the
same warns in it. The report keeps the checks only once the waits are on its Loop line: when the loop hook
fails or times out, or the Loop line reads `not read`, the group is empty and those warns are "unexpected".

A FAIL is never "yours", and no wait names a `launchd.*` or `config.*` check, so they stay "unexpected" (a
`launchd.*` warn reads the same for a harmless drift and for a job that exits 64 on every run). "yours" is not
"expected": the Doctor section still shows the line with its fix or note, and no warn changes the outcome.
`unexpected N` counts every other warn and every FAIL, so on a Mac with such a wait it drops by the yours
count while `N warn` stays; compare warn totals, or `yours + unexpected`, across reports.

Why: the report said "yours" in its Doctor section and "unexpected" in its Summary for a wait its own Loop line
listed two lines above, on every round, which trains a reader to skip the word meant to catch a stopped
background sync. Amends §16.14 (dated lines there, in K16b and in the `ReportHooks` and `NextStep` blocks) and
§16.37 (dated line there). Tests: `tests/test_loop.py`
(`test_checks_name_the_doctor_check_each_wait_explains`), `tests/test_setup_report.py`
(`test_a_wait_the_loop_names_is_yours_and_a_stopped_sync_stays_unexpected`,
`test_no_yours_group_without_the_loops_checks`, `test_no_yours_group_when_the_loop_line_is_not_read`,
`test_an_empty_cloud_folders_heartbeat_is_yours_through_the_cli`).

#### N22: status's inbox part is about the kept inbox (`agentsync.loop`)

`status`'s `inbox on|missing|off` (`loop.status_line`) is about the inbox the guides name: the live inbox source
on the folder `config.ensure_inbox` keeps (`canonical_source_root(<docs repo's parent folder>/inbox)`), else every
live inbox source, the same choice `publish.Publisher.root_guide` makes. A hand-added inbox source whose folder is
