gone is doctor's `source.<id>.listable` FAIL in the same `status` output, with exit 1, and no longer makes the
part read `inbox missing` while the kept inbox is there. The three words and `inbox ?` are unchanged.

Rejected: `missing` or `off` when no live source is on the kept folder. The guide then names the other inbox
sources as the drop folder, so `on` answers whether the folders it names exist, and no `[FAIL]` line would
explain another word. Also rejected: moving `root_guide`'s selection into a shared helper, a refactor of
pinned guide output that the fix does not need; the test pins the shared meaning instead.

Why: the part read `inbox missing` on a Mac whose kept inbox existed, because sources added by hand pointed at
folders that were gone (triage 2026-10-08), the one place that still used the older meaning. Amends §16.21
item 2 and the note in §16.36 (dated lines there). Test: `tests/test_loop.py`
(`test_status_line_inbox_is_the_kept_inbox_not_every_inbox_source`).

#### N34: the baseline NEXT names the docs repo's AGENTS.md too (`agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.setup_report`)

Rules 4, 6 and 8's NEXT lines name the docs repo's root AGENTS.md by its path after the skill's section:
`... the agentsync-docs skill's "Baseline questions" section (also in ~/agent-context/docs/AGENTS.md), then
run ...` (`loop._baseline`; the path is the configured docs repo's, written as `loop._shown` writes every path
here). The setup report's Loop line shows it as `AGENTS.md`, its last part like every path on that line,
whatever the docs repo's path (`_eval_by_name`, since a path with a space would otherwise leave its tail).

Why: an agent that loads no skill was sent only to the skill, while the section it needs is in the root guide
`publish.root_guide` writes as AGENTS.md (bring-back 2026-10-06, row 23). A bare `AGENTS.md` would be the
agent's own project's file when it runs `agentsync sync` from another folder. The path adds no value to a
report: its Configuration part already names the docs repo. Amends §12 item 12 and §16.20 (dated lines
there). Tests: `tests/test_loop.py` (`test_the_baseline_next_names_the_agents_md_that_carries_the_section`),
`tests/test_setup_report.py` (`test_the_loop_line_keeps_no_part_of_a_docs_repo_path_with_spaces`).

#### N24: the lock-held warning names its holder (`agentsync.cli`, `agentsync.errors`, `agentsync.ops.lock`, `agentsync.cycle`)

A run refused the lock (exit 75) logs `WARNING agentsync.cli: skipped: lock held by <who>`. `<who>` is
`LockHeldError.who`: the holder's lock label (`poll`, `reconcile`, `dry_run`, `governance`), or `an
unidentified holder (empty lock body)` or `an unidentified holder (unparseable lock body)`; the body is empty
between a holder's flock and its body write. The holder's pid, start time, host, beat and stage stay on the
stderr line `skipped: lock held (lock held: <full holder>)`, which has no level word and is unchanged.
`LockHeldError(holder, *, who=None)`: `who` defaults to `holder`, and `str(exc)` and `.holder` are as before.
The interactive wait's re-raise carries `who` through and no longer doubles the `lock held:` prefix. No
command, flag, option or key is added.
**Amended (2026-10-11, §16.49, B13 round 2 R62):** the body is also empty for the whole of install.sh's
reinstall, which holds the lock through lockf (§16.41 "The reinstall holds the background sync's lock") for up to
its 120 s wait plus the uv run, and for an `is_held` probe. §16.41 N6 changed the stderr line for an empty body to
`an unrecorded holder (install.sh while it reinstalls agentsync, or a check for an instant)`, so the stderr line
is no longer unchanged there. `<who>` for an empty body is now those same fixed words, so the WARNING reads
`skipped: lock held by an unrecorded holder (install.sh while it reinstalls agentsync, or a check for an
instant)`; a body that does not parse keeps `an unidentified holder (unparseable lock body)`. The text is still
a constant, so Recent errors still merges it (one new entry once, when the text changed). doctor's lock line
adds `(a cycle is running)` only when the held lock has a body: with none it reads `held by an unrecorded
holder (...)`.
**Amended 2026-10-13, §16.68 H33:** a cycle label (`poll`, `reconcile`, `dry_run`) is now rendered `another sync
(its pass: <label>)` in the WARNING, since a sync typed in a terminal holds the lock as `poll` too; `who` itself
is unchanged, and the text is still one constant per label, so Recent errors still merges it.

Why the label alone: the setup report's Recent errors keeps only lines with a level word, so the holder was
on a line it drops, and it merges only lines that read the same after their time (§16.36). The beat and its
age change on every skip, and the pid and start time on every run of the holder, so where a reconcile and a
poll collide each hour, or at each wake, one entry per run filled the 40-entry window (measured in design: 43
entries against 1) and pushed out the other errors. The merged entry's count and its first and last time
still tell a stuck holder from repeated slow runs. Amends §9 step 2 (dated line there) and the §15 copies of
`LockHeldError` and `EXIT_LOCK_HELD`. Tests: `tests/test_cli.py`
(`test_lock_held_warning_names_the_holder_and_repeats_verbatim`), `tests/test_ops_lock.py`
(`test_second_instance_in_same_process_is_refused`,
`test_a_holder_with_no_lock_body_yet_is_named_as_unidentified`).
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R50:** an empty body reads `an unrecorded holder (install.sh while it reinstalls
agentsync, a status or doctor check, or a cycle starting)` in `who`, in the stderr line and in doctor alike
(one constant, `agentsync.ops.lock.EMPTY_BODY_HOLDER`); install.sh's lockf, an `is_held` probe and a cycle
between its flock and its body write all leave the body empty. A non-empty body that does not parse keeps `an
unidentified holder (unparseable lock body)`.

#### N26: the empty-cloud-folder wait and the report count the files the last walk did not list (`agentsync.manifest`, `agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.setup_report`)

`Manifest.unlisted_count(source_id, *, since=0) -> int`: the source's present file rows whose `last_seen_run`
is below the run of its newest FULL `run_sources` row and at or above `since`. It is 0 when there is no such
row, or when that row recorded an error (a pass that failed after its walk and before its transaction
committed has the row and stamped no item, so every file would count).

When that count is above 0, an empty-cloud-folder wait (§16.22) ends with `the last walk of <id> did not list N
file(s) the mirror still has: once the listing is complete, later syncs take out the pages of those still
absent, with the usual deletion check`. `since` is the run in manifest meta `scope_root:<id>` (0 when it is
missing or unreadable; `loop._missed`), because a complete pass retires a row last listed under an earlier
`path` as a scope change and does not check it. The clause appears once per source, on its last line: on the
line about folders that held mirrored files as `; in all, ...` when the source has one (removing those folders
is what completes the listing, and that line's own count is among the N), otherwise on the paste line as
`; ...`. It gives a count, never a path, and never mentions a purge (one is queued only under
`gov.purge_on_upstream_delete`). The wait for a folder that could not be listed gets no clause: its advice
includes an exclude, which retires the rows under it at once.

The setup report's per-source Empty cloud folders line (§16.28) ends, after `... below M of the checked
folder(s)`, with one of `; its last walk did not list U of the T file(s) the mirror holds for it`, `; no walk
of it is recorded`, or `; its last walk ended on an error, so the files it did not list are not counted`.
(**amended 2026-10-11, §16.47 R14:** a fourth ending, `; its last walk listed all T file(s) the mirror holds for
it`, replaces the first when U is 0.)
There is no `since` there: the report states the fact, so the two counts can differ only after a `path`
change.

Known limit: between an edit to sources.toml and the next sync both counts are against the last walk, as the
wait's folders are; the next sync rewrites them. In an inbox (N27) both counts also include a mirrored file
that is still there but that the last walk withheld as changed within `quiescence_s` (or future-dated): a
withheld item is not in the listing, so its row is not stamped. Nothing is taken out for it (the clause
promises only "those still absent"), and the first sync that lists the file drops it from the count. The
withheld set is not stored per walk, so the count cannot leave it out
(`test_an_inbox_file_the_walk_withheld_is_in_the_count_until_a_sync_lists_it`).
**Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R101:** a pass stamps `last_seen_run`, and only that, on the present file rows
of the files its walk withheld (`ScanResult.withheld`, `Manifest.touch_withheld`), so neither count includes a
withheld file that is still there, and `unseen_live` never offers one as a deletion candidate. A withheld file
with no row (a new file still being written) stamps nothing, so a file deleted upstream still counts. N27's
parenthetical that an inbox's count includes such a file no longer holds
(`test_an_inbox_file_the_walk_withheld_is_not_in_the_count`,
`test_withheld_inbox_files_leave_a_real_deletion_in_the_count`).

Why: with a listing held incomplete, files deleted upstream stay mirrored and no line said how many
(rehearsal v10, `unchanged=26` beside `live 30`), so the person pasting the exclude line could not tell what
completing the listing would check. Amends §16.22 and the report's Empty cloud folders paragraph (dated lines
there). Tests: `tests/test_loop.py`
(`test_the_exclude_wait_counts_the_mirrored_files_the_walk_did_not_list`,
`test_a_pass_that_failed_after_its_walk_counts_no_file_as_not_listed`,
`test_an_empty_cloud_folder_that_held_mirrored_files_gets_no_exclude_line`), `tests/test_setup_report.py`
(`test_empty_cloud_folders_part_says_which_are_dataless_without_listing_one`).

#### N27: empty cloud folders: the alarm, an inbox, and the WAITING ON YOU lines (`agentsync.arm_local`, `agentsync.loop`, `agentsync.ops.doctor`)

Whenever a local or inbox walk found an empty cloud folder below the root, the scan's alarm no longer offers an
exclude:
- all unknown folders empty: `N unknown dir(s) — empty cloud folder(s), zero children in a cloud tree: ...;
  enumeration incomplete, no deletions this pass (each WAITING ON YOU line about <id> says what to do, and
  agentsync status prints them)`, for an inbox as for a local source;
- mixed with another cause: the old cause, then `(grant the agent Files and Folders access for the other
  folders; for the empty ones, each WAITING ON YOU line about <id> says what to do, and agentsync status prints
  them)`;
- no empty cloud folder below the root (an unreadable folder, a provider error, an empty cloud root): the old
  text, byte for byte.
  **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R103:** an empty root, cloud or plain, gets one alarm and no exclude advice:
  with files mirrored, `source root <root> is empty but N file(s) are mirrored (unmounted volume?): enumeration
  incomplete, nothing is deleted`; an empty cloud root with nothing mirrored, `source root <root> has zero
  children in a cloud tree: enumeration incomplete, nothing is deleted`. A root that cannot be listed keeps the
  old cause, with the advice `(grant the agent Files and Folders access)` only.

An inbox whose newest FULL pass stored empty cloud folders that today's `exclude` does not prune gets the
local source's two waits (§16.22), with N26's count (which in an inbox also includes a present file the last
walk withheld as still being written: N26, Known limit), since another sync does not clear them: the paste line
only for folders with nothing mirrored below them (an inbox's default `exclude` is all always-excluded names,
so its list is the folders alone), and the line about folders that held mirrored files, whose step is the
person's. Its `heartbeat.<id>` check is then among `NextStep.checks`. Any other incomplete inbox keeps one
`note:`, which no longer says "a later sync lists it": `the inbox (<ids>) was not fully listed: a later sync
lists a file that was still being written, but not a folder it cannot read or an empty cloud folder
(\`agentsync sync -v\` names the cause); it does not block the next step`. Doctor's local heartbeat fix reads
"each WAITING ON YOU line about <id>". No pointer uses nested parentheses (doctor's fix parser strips one
level).

Why: in the mixed case the alarm said "exclude a deliberately empty cloud folder" two lines above the wait
that warns such an exclude retires pages with no deletion check; "a later sync lists it" was false for an
empty cloud folder, an empty cloud inbox root and a folder the walk cannot read, and a step only the person
can take belongs in a wait (install.sh, the setup report's Loop line and the setup prompt show waits, not
notes); "the WAITING ON YOU line" sat above two lines when a source had both kinds of folder. Rejected: an
inbox-only note telling the person to remove the folders, which drops the "if the files were removed on
purpose" condition for a folder whose removal lets held deletions through. Not changed: an empty cloud source
root still gets the old alarm's exclude advice, though a root cannot be excluded. **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45
R103:** it no longer does: an empty root, cloud or plain, gets the empty-root alarm alone (the bullet above).
Amends §16.20, §16.22 and
§16.37 (dated lines in §16.20, §16.22 and §16.37). Tests: `tests/test_arm_local.py`
(`test_zero_child_cloud_dirs_log_at_info_and_the_scan_alarm_names_them`,
`test_an_unreadable_folder_beside_an_empty_cloud_folder_offers_no_exclude`,
`test_an_inbox_empty_cloud_folder_alarm_points_at_the_waits`), `tests/test_loop.py`
(`test_an_empty_cloud_folder_in_an_inbox_gets_the_waits_of_a_local_source`,
`test_an_inbox_listing_left_incomplete_by_no_empty_folder_promises_nothing`), `tests/test_ops_doctor.py`.

#### N28: a folder the walk cannot list is one warning a walk (`agentsync.arm_local`)

`walk` logs each folder whose listing fails (EPERM or EACCES from the privacy grant, EDEADLK or ETIMEDOUT from
the file provider, ENOENT for a folder gone mid-walk) at info, as it already does a zero-child cloud folder.
Once a walk, including a walk stopped by a held listing, it logs one warning naming those folders with their
reasons, the first five in sorted order and a count of the rest (`_warn_unlisted`): `<id>: N folder(s) could
not be listed: 'Locked' (EACCES: Permission denied)`, then ` (+K more)`. Empty cloud folders are not in it, so
five of them sorting first do not push a failed folder out of the line. A background job logs at warning and
the scan's alarm is not logged (§16.22's "logged at warning" holds only for the alarms of a scan that ends
early), so this line is the one that brings the reason to the job's log and to the setup report's Recent
errors, which scrubs the names to `'<path>'` and keeps the reason. The alarm text, `WalkStats`, STATE.md and
the per-entry `cannot lstat` warning are unchanged.

Why: the per-folder warning repeated on every poll, since a local walk is always a full pass, and filled the
64 KiB of the job's log that Recent errors reads. Rejected: only lowering the line to info, which leaves no
line with the reason in a background job's log; and logging the whole alarm with reasons, which names the
first five unknown folders of any kind (five empty ones hide the failed one) and is longer than the line it
replaces for one to three folders. Amends §16.22 (dated line there). Tests: `tests/test_arm_local.py`
(`test_unlistable_folders_log_at_info_and_one_warning_names_them_with_their_reason`,
`test_a_held_listing_still_warns_about_the_folders_it_could_not_list`), `tests/test_setup_report.py`
(`test_recent_errors_never_carry_an_item_path_or_document_name`).

### 16.40 Setup report fixes (2026-10-11, wave B13 lane C)

**The MDM server's host is `<mdmhost>`** (B13 N39; amends the v4 revision's 2026-10-10 amendment). `enrollment()`
registers it as kind `mdmhost` (unnumbered; legend `<mdmhost> MDM server's host`, right after `<host> this Mac's
host or computer name`), and the shell fallback's `redaction_pairs` uses the same placeholder and its Redaction
paragraph names it. The whole host is replaced, and no vendor suffix is kept. A host equal to a value already
registered keeps that value's placeholder. The kind is one word: a hyphen in a placeholder means a number, and a
word boundary inside it would let a shorter value (`mdm`, `host`) match there when a line is redacted twice (the
Summary's item lines are, by `_item_line` and then by the whole report).

**A value matches in either Unicode form** (B13 N7, rehearsal v10fix3: `Café Plans` in clear). A Finder-made name
is NFD on disk and an agent types it NFC, or the reverse. The Redactor keys every value by its NFC form (`_norm`
normalises after the backslashes go, since one between a letter and its accent stops composition) and `_compile`
matches each literal as written, in NFC and in NFD, judging its word edges on the NFC form, where an accented last
letter is a letter and not a combining mark. One folder seen in both forms is one placeholder. The shell
fallback's `add_pair` emits the NFC and NFD forms (`/usr/bin/iconv`, `UTF-8-MAC`) of a value that is not
printable ASCII, after the one length gate on the value as written, so every caller (organisation, folder, full
name and its tokens) gets both forms. Tests: `test_a_folder_name_is_redacted_in_either_unicode_form` and
`test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_folder_in_either_unicode_form`. Out of scope: an accent-stripped ASCII spelling
(`Cafe Plans`, a different word), one string mixing both forms, and a `$'..'` word the shell reader does not decode.

**Proxy values: the PAC URL after its scheme, and git's proxies** (B13 H19, H1 skeptic C2). A cloud proxy's PAC
path can name the customer (`/<domain>/proxy.pac`, `?customer=`), and agentsync prints the PAC URL whole (doctor's
`network.proxy` line, the policy error, the Environment line). The report registers the system PAC URL after its
scheme as one `<proxy-N>` value beside its host, so it is redacted where agentsync prints it and where it is quoted
without the scheme; the scheme stays visible (`https://<proxy-2>`). It also registers the `proxy =` values in the
config files git reads (`~/.gitconfig`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config`, `/etc/gitconfig` and the `.git/config` of
the installed checkout, the one `direct_url.json` names, and of the checkout the prompt clones,
`~/src/agent-context-sync`), read as files with no git process, because a git error logged at step 1 names git's
proxy (`Could not resolve proxy: <host>`) and step 1 may have stopped with no git. One reader,
`_git_proxy_urls`, serves this and §16.43's H1; its values are registered after every other proxy value, the PAC
URL after its scheme included, so a git-only proxy leaves the other `<proxy-N>` numbers as they were. The shell fallback's `redaction_pairs`
registers the same PAC value, the PAC URL's host and the host of every proxy URL that has a dot (scutil, the
proxy environment variables, `[network] proxy` and the same git config files, its own checkout standing for the
installed one), cutting the path before the userinfo, as `urlsplit` does. This supersedes §16.43's sentence
that the shell fallback report does not read git's config yet. Redaction only grows. Tests:
`test_a_pac_url_is_redacted_after_its_scheme`, `test_a_proxy_in_any_git_config_file_is_redacted`,
`test_a_proxy_only_git_knows_is_redacted`, `test_the_shell_report_redacts_the_pac_url_and_proxy_hosts` and
`test_the_shell_report_reads_every_git_config_file_in_a_utf8_locale`. Not changed: the Python report still
registers a dotless proxy host, and the LaunchAgent's own proxy (`launchctl getenv`) is printed but not
registered. **Amended (2026-10-12, §16.46 "Proxies" R42/R67 and R68, §16.47 R110):** the shell now registers a
dotless proxy host too (R42/R67), both reports read a linked worktree's `<common dir>/config` and `<git
dir>/config.worktree` besides `.git/config` (R110), and the LaunchAgent's own proxy is registered (R68). An empty `proxy =` (git's way to turn a proxy off) registers nothing: the
match stays on its own line, and does not take the next line's first token (`[user]`, `sslVerify`). A proxy value
that `urlsplit` rejects (`http://[x`) is skipped. Before this, either case made the whole redactor fail, so the
report fell back to redacting the home folder only. Tests: `test_an_unreadable_proxy_value_keeps_the_redaction`
(the whole report) and `test_an_empty_git_proxy_takes_no_token_from_the_next_line` (the pattern alone: with the
`urlsplit` guard, a pattern that reached across the line break would still leave the report redacted). Lane F's
`test_an_empty_git_proxy_takes_no_line_after_it` asserted what the first one's `empty-git-proxy` case asserts and
is merged into it.

**A bracketed part or a middle part does not hide the first and last name** (B13 N8; amends the v5 revision's
2026-10-10 amendment on full names). The registrations from the whole field are unchanged. The name without its
bracketed part ("Doe, Jane (Contoso)", "Jane (JJ) Doe") adds a fuzzy value, and so do, in the order the name is
said ("Jane Q. Doe" for "Doe, Jane Q."), its words joined without their dots and every two of its words in either
order, the later of 2 or more characters and the earlier the first word or of 2 or more: a middle part, a suffix
("Jane Doe, Jr.", said "Jr. Jane Doe") or a title ("Dr. Jane Doe") no longer hides `jane-doe`, `JaneDoe` or
`doe-jane`, in either report. (Pairing only the first word with the others left a suffix or a title as the first
word, so the shell fallback, which has no comma-part forms, printed `jane-doe` in clear for "Jane Doe, Jr.".)
A bracketed part's words of 3 or more characters, without the brackets, are lone names (written and upper-case
forms), registered after every other value, so a tail that is the organisation stays `<org-N>` bare and joined
(`<org-1>-sales`). The shell fallback registers each word as written and without its brackets, leaves the bracketed
part out of the joined forms the same way and matches those forms as written, lower case and upper case, with a
space, `-`, `_` or nothing between the words; it matches no other mix of case and does not upper-case a letter
outside ASCII. The shell fallback now emits the login before the name, so a login that is the name run together
stays `<user>` (K9); before, the shell had no joined form for it to collide with. Its Redaction paragraph says "the
full name and its joined forms (`<name>`)". Tests:
`test_a_bracketed_tail_or_a_middle_part_does_not_hide_the_first_and_last_name`,
`test_a_bracketed_tail_that_is_the_organisation_stays_org`, `test_a_bracketed_part_of_two_letters_stays_a_name`,
`test_the_shell_report_redacts_the_joined_forms_of_a_display_name` and
`test_the_shell_report_shows_a_login_that_is_the_name_run_together_as_user`. Not covered: nested brackets ("Jane
Doe (Contoso (EU))" keeps the outer part in the core; first plus last is still registered).

**A two-letter name part is a lone name too** (B13 H20; replaces the v5 revision's sentence on a first part of 2
characters). Any part of the name, comma or not, that has two letters and starts with a capital is also a lone
name, in its written and upper-case forms ("Li" and "LI" for "Li, Jane" or "Jane Li"). No form that the report's
own lines or an agent's sentences use is registered: any case of a sentence-opening word, title, suffix or mail
prefix (`_SHORT_WORDS`: "No", "An", "Do", "He", "Jr", "Re"), and the upper case of an abbreviation or numeral
(`_SHORT_CAPS`: "AI", "OU", "II"). So "Ai" is a lone name and "AI" is not. A part like "Do" is redacted only
inside the joined forms. A part written in lower case ("de", "la") is a particle and is never a lone name: alone
it names no one, and registered it would turn `ls -la` into `ls -<name>`. The shell fallback registers a two-letter
part by the same rule and the same lists (`short_name`, the written form, whole words); its joined forms come from
the N8 entry above. Tests: `test_a_two_letter_name_part_is_a_lone_name_unless_the_report_uses_it`,
`test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_two_letter_name_part` and `test_the_shell_short_name_lists_are_the_reports` (the
two lists are the same in both places). Held: a two-letter name that is a listed word ("He", "An", "Do") stays
redacted only inside the joined forms, since alone it would replace the report's words; an all-capitals GECOS
("LI, JANE") registers "LI" only.

**A CloudStorage folder of any provider registers its organisation** (B13 N9; amends the v4 revision's redaction
values). macOS names a `~/Library/CloudStorage` folder `<app>-<domain>`. Both reports register the part after the
app's name as `<org-N>` (fuzzy in the Python report), for every provider and not only `OneDrive-`; a leading
`SharedLibraries-` is dropped. Not registered: a bare app name (`Dropbox`), `Personal`, `Business` and `Work`, and
a part equal to the app's name (`Box-Box`). The Python report leaves a part that the email pattern matches whole to
that pattern, which turns the whole folder name into `<email-N>`; any other part with `@` is an `<org-N>`. The
shell fallback, which has no email pattern, registers an address part as `<org-N>` too. Hidden entries (a leading
dot) are skipped, as in the Environment line. The Python report registers the `OneDrive-` organisations first, so
`<org-1>` stays the OneDrive organisation, and its residue check skips the app name before a registered folder's
`<org-N>` (`Dropbox-<org-2>` is no hit; `residue(..., ignore=)`, `_Run.provider_heads`). `it-request`'s `<org>`
is unchanged (OneDrive only: it is the Entra organisation). Why: a `Dropbox-<team>` folder printed verbatim in the
Environment line and in install.log's `--source-local` arguments, and the shell report printed a Google Drive
account's address. The shell's Redaction paragraph and `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md`'s `<org-N>` row say so.
Tests: `test_org_of_takes_the_part_after_any_providers_app_name`,
`test_a_dropbox_team_folder_is_an_org_and_its_app_name_no_residue` and
`test_the_shell_report_redacts_any_providers_team_and_account`. Trade-off: a domain that is an ordinary word
(`SynologyDrive-Home`-shaped) is replaced wherever the word appears, as the OneDrive organisation already is; the
shell numbers its organisations in glob order, so its `<org-N>` can differ from the Python report's.

**The redaction count is what the report shows** (B13 N31). The count was of replacement events, and the text a
reader sees differed from it both ways. A source's label (`_Labels.of`) is replaced once and cached per id, so it
was counted once and shown in every row for that source (a field report: 182 replacements counted, source 119,
against 175 `<source-N>` shown). A friction item is redacted and then cut short (`_item_line`, `_shorten`), and
`_source_local_shown` redacts pieces of an argument and may then cut it to `<path>`, so replacements in the
cut-off part were counted and not shown. Rule: `build_report` calls `Redactor.recount(main)` once, on the redacted
report before its Redaction section, and each numbered placeholder (`<kind-N>`, `_NUMBERED_RE`) counts as often as
that text shows it; `values` keeps only the numbered placeholders it shows. The unnumbered kinds (home, user, name,
serial, host, mdmhost, tmp) keep their replacement count, because the report writes `~/` paths and template fields
such as the IT request's `<serial>` itself, so a count of them in the text would not be a redaction count. The
Summary's `- redaction:` line, the Redaction section's line and the CLI's "wrote ..." line all carry the recounted
numbers. `recount` is one pass over the text (`findall`), since up to `_LISTING_MAX` folder names are registered:
2,039 placeholders over 442 KB took 1.2 ms that way against about 1 s with one `str.count` each. The Redaction
section's count line adds: "Numbered placeholders are counted each time this report shows them; the unnumbered
kinds (...) each time a value was replaced, a line cut short afterwards included, because the report also writes
~/ paths and template fields of its own." The kind list is built from `_LEGEND` and `_UNNUMBERED`, and the sentence
writes no literal unnumbered placeholder. Rejected: counting `~` and `<serial>` in the text (they are the report's
own words too); fixing each cache and cut at its source (a new one would bring the drift back); sentinel
characters around placeholders (every reader of redacted text would have to strip them). The shell fallback
prints no count, so it has no twin. Tests: `test_recount_counts_numbered_placeholders_in_the_text_and_leaves_the_rest`
and `test_the_redaction_count_is_the_placeholders_the_report_shows`. Rehearsal triage will see the number rise
(the field report's 182 would be about 238).
Amended 2026-10-13, §16.64 G3: the sentence reads "Numbered placeholders are counted each time this report shows
one. The unnumbered kinds (...) are counted each time a value was replaced, even in a line that was cut short
later, because the report also writes ~/ paths and template fields of its own, and those are not replacements."

**A run with no end line says whether its process is gone** (B13 H14 and N33; amends §16.28's Installer
paragraph and §16.14's outcome detail). No trap sees a SIGKILL, so a killed run keeps its start line and the step
lines that had ended, and has no end line; install.sh writes a step's line when the step ends, so the step under
way has none. The run id ends in install.sh's `$$`, and the report runs on the Mac that wrote it, so the report
probes that pid with signal 0 (`_pid_alive`, in the probes block; `_RUN_PID_RE` and `_open_state` beside
`_reached`). Signal 0 sends nothing, and only runs with no end line are probed, so the report stays read-only.
No such process reads `its process is gone: killed, or the Mac restarted` (HUP, INT and TERM log 129, 130 and
143, so a run with no end line whose process is gone was killed, or the Mac stopped) (**amended 2026-10-11,
§16.47 R131:** it reads `its process is gone: killed, the Mac restarted, or its end line could not be written`:
`log_at` drops a write that fails, so a run that exited on a full disk leaves no end line either, and no record
of why); a process that exists, also
another user's, reads `its process id is in use: still running, or the id was reused`; a run id with no pid, or a
pid of 0 or 1, keeps `interrupted, or still running`. The pid is read and never printed. The state is in the
per-run status (`no end line (<state>)`), the Summary's `- install.sh:` line and the outcome detail (`install.sh
has no end line (<state>; last failed step <step>)`; the outcome kind and step are unchanged). The bullet under
`Runs with no end line` reads `- run <id>: started <t>, <state>; the last of its N step line(s) is <step
(result)>, and nothing after it is logged (a step's line is written when the step ends, so a step under way has
none)`, or `it has no step line (...)`. (**amended 2026-10-11, §16.47 R107:** `the last of its N step lines is`
for two or more, and `its only step line is <step (result)>` for one.) It never says a run reached a step: the step under way when a run stops
has no line, and the run reported as having "reached launcher" was in `helpers` (v10 E1 run B1). install.log's
format is unchanged. Rejected: an end line written for the dead run by the next run (it would invent an exit
that `retried_runs` and the seconds total count), a line at each step's start (it doubles the step lines every
reader counts), and naming the next step from a fixed order (older installers had no `helpers` step). Tests:
`test_a_run_with_no_end_line_says_whether_its_process_is_gone`,
`test_a_run_with_no_end_line_and_a_failed_step_keeps_the_two_apart`,
`test_a_run_cut_off_in_a_step_names_the_last_step_logged`, `test_pid_alive_reads_this_process_and_a_reaped_one`
and `test_a_run_killed_during_the_helper_builds_reads_as_killed`. Accepted: a reused pid reads as "in use",
which keeps both readings, as before.

**The "nothing started since" note says install.log** (B13 H17; amends §16.37). The note said "no install.sh
run began since attempt <N> finished", but the report it sits in is written by `install.sh --report-only` (step 3,
or by hand), which logs no run in install.log (`log_at` returns under `--report-only`; install.sh's header: "never
a dry run or --report-only"), so an install.sh run wrote a report saying none began. The condition is install.log's
runs (a `--list-folders` run counts), so the note now says what it read: `- note: no attempt was started and
install.log has no run that began since attempt <N> finished at <end>, more than 10 minutes before this report
(install.log does not log `install.sh --report-only`), so this report is of attempt <N>. A later session whose
step 1 command stopped before `install.sh --log-start` (no Xcode tools, a git failure) and logged nothing is not
in it.` The condition, the outcome, the issue link and the installer's output are unchanged; `bring-back.md`
copies the Summary, so it carries the new words. Rejected: logging `--report-only` in install.log so the old words
become true. The `--report-only` run that writes the report would then always start after the end line, so the
note would never fire in either case it exists for, and every install.log reader would see a run with no step.
Test: `test_a_report_long_after_the_last_attempt_says_no_attempt_was_started_since`.

**The install source's commit skips a run that read no commit** (B13 N20, triage 2026-10-08 D4.b; amends K6).
The Summary's `last install.sh run: commit <sha>` is now the start line of the last run that reached an install
step, meaning a run with a step line other than `report` and `list-folders`. install.sh computes and logs the
commit just before its first install step (`step_start uv`), and `report` (from the EXIT trap) and `list-folders`
are the only steps a run can log without getting there, so the rule is exactly "this start line's `commit=` was
computed". A `--list-folders` run logs `commit=- kind=- source=-`, and a usage error logs `commit=-` whether it came
before the source was resolved (`kind=-`) or after it (`--source-local` with a folder that does not exist logs
`kind=checkout commit=-`); none of them installed anything, and each turned the line into `commit -`, also in the
`--report-only` report that follows it. A run killed during the uv step has no step line and is skipped; it
installed nothing. An install run that logged `commit=-` (a checkout on a Mac with no developer tools) still says
`commit -`. That is why the rule is not "the last start line with a commit", which would show an older run's
commit as the last one's. The label `last install.sh run` stays. Test:
`test_install_source_skips_a_run_that_read_no_commit`.

**A v6 install-step error is resolved as v7's, and the Summary's installer output is this attempt's** (B13
H21, v10 E3.b and E3.h; amends §16.14, §16.22 and §16.30). `stopping_error` resolves an install-step error of a v6
attempt by any install run of the attempt that ended rc 0, whenever the line was logged, as since §16.22 for v7.
§16.22 kept v6's rule because its step 2 also started background sync. But that was the one install.sh command,
whose exit 0 required the background job to be running (`--confirm-install-agent`: in every installer a v6 copy
could reach step 2 with, `35c2b5f` to `7c4fbf2`, anything short of a running background job exits 1, or 3 while
Allow is pending; since v8 the installer stops a v6 copy at step 1), and v6 after K11b started none. A step 2
`error` an agent logged after a successful install therefore read "failed at step 2" in every later report from a
Mac with such an attempt. A step 1 error still needs a run started at or after it; v5 keeps its `end`-line rule;
`retried_runs` stays v7-only. The Summary's `installer output:` line counts from the first install.out header
(`# run=<id>`) whose id is a run of the latest attempt (`runs_for_attempt`), when that attempt has a time: the
attempt's runs are the file's last, so "in the last <n> line(s)" still holds, and the line adds "(this attempt's
runs only: the <k> earlier run(s) read are not counted; the Installer section counts them)". No run of the
attempt in what was read: "- installer output: no run of this attempt in the last <n> line(s) of install.out (the
Installer section counts the <r> earlier run(s) read)". With no friction log, an attempt with no time, no header
read, no run in install.log (nothing then says when the runs read happened), or every run read the attempt's, the
line is as before. The Installer section's line still counts every whole run read. `_OUT_RUN_RE` captures the run
id, `_Facts.out_counted` keeps the lines counted, and `_installer_output_line` writes the Summary's line. The next
triage of a report from a Mac with such a v6 attempt sees it move from "failed at step 2" to "fully one command"
or "worked with help": that is this fix, not a new event. Tests:
`test_the_summary_counts_the_installer_output_of_the_latest_attempts_runs_only` and
`test_v6_an_install_step_error_is_resolved_by_an_install_run_that_ended_0`.

**The first-sync count names the field it counts** (B13 N17, field triage 2026-10-07 U18 and 2026-10-08 D1.h;
amends §16.14 and §16.37). The clause read "N of M source(s) listed completely (status: baseline complete) at
least once by the time this report was written". "listed completely" names status's other field (`complete
yes|no`, the last listing), not the one counted (`baseline complete|INCOMPLETE`), and readers took it as every
source listed. It now reads "N of M source(s) with a complete baseline (status, read when this report was
written)". The count is unchanged: the sources status shows `baseline complete`, of those it lists. A baseline is
set by a complete listing and cleared only by a scope change, so a source showing `baseline complete · complete
no` has one and is counted, and the words claim nothing about the first sync itself. Test:
`test_first_sync_doctor_warns_and_it_draft_in_the_summary`.

**The first-sync line counts what other runs read again** (B13 N32, v10 E3-verifier E3.c; amends §16.14's
first-sync line and §16.37's "The first sync's read-again count reaches the report"). When runs other than the
installer's sync read files again since that install run began, the Summary's first-sync line ends `· since this
install run began, [at least ]N read(s) again by K other run(s) (the newest is run <id>; the background job's runs
and syncs typed in a terminal are recorded alike: see the OCR part)`.
- N is the sum of the run records' `reread` over those runs, the OCR part's unit: a file read in two runs counts
  twice. `_ocr_time` keeps each run it read in `_Facts.runs_read`; no new query.
- The installer's sync is a run that started inside its first-sync step (the step line's stamp, its seconds and
  one second of slack) and keeps its own `read again R`. A skipped step ran no sync.
- Another run that started inside the step is left out with it, for example a poll that took the lock just
  before the installer's sync, which waits for it. So N can fall short, but it never counts the installer's
  re-reads twice.
- The line says `at least` when all 200 runs the report reads started after the install began.
- Nothing is added when no such run read again, or when the OCR part did not run.
- A run record does not say who started the run, so the line never says background.

Why: the v10 report's clause read `converted 0, deferred 0` while a poll during the helpers step had read 17
files again, and only the OCR part showed it. No command, flag or key. `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md` has a
`first sync:` row. Test: `test_the_first_sync_line_counts_what_other_runs_read_again_since_the_install`.

**The first-sync line says `sync:` after a config that already existed** (B13 N25, v10 E3-verifier; amends
§16.22). The Summary's line starts `- sync:` when the install run whose first-sync step it reads logged its config
step with note `add-source` or `exists` (sources.toml existed before that run), as install.sh's own lines do since
2026-10-06 (§16.22); else `- first sync:` (note `created`, no config step, or no run). The label and the numbers
come from the same run. A run that created the config and whose sync failed, followed by a run that found it,
reads `- sync:`, as that second run printed; the `- install.sh:` line beside it shows both runs. The install.log
step stays `first-sync`, and the `- install.sh:` step list, the outcome text and install.sh's error texts still
name it so. `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md` lists both forms. Test:
`test_the_first_sync_line_says_sync_when_the_config_existed`.

**The OCR part has a speech line** (B13 H18, B12 E3.e; amends §16.28). `- speech: <state> (<detail>)` follows
`- media helper:`, in the same words (`ready`, `off`, `not built`, `failed`, `did not answer within 1.5s`, `not
measured (...)`), from `convert.speech.probe`, the call Doctor's speech check makes, with its own `_PROBE_S`
(1.5 s) wait that is not counted against the evidence parts (`_Mirror.not_counted`). The media and speech lines
share `_helper_line`. The label is `speech`, as the installer and Doctor print it. Why: the 2026-10-10 report
showed the speech engine nowhere but the agent's friction line; Doctor lists an ok `speech` by name only, and the
installer's line is past the 60 lines of install.out the report keeps. A hung speech helper costs the report up
to 1.5 s more of its 12 s, as a hung media helper does. No command, flag or key. Test:
`test_the_ocr_part_has_a_speech_line_of_its_own`.

**The Summary names the draft baseline's folder in words** (B13 N18, v9 defect 6, v10 rehearsals; amends §16.32
"In the setup report" and "Whatever the docs repo's path", and, by a dated line added 2026-10-11 (§16.49, R61),
§16.37's "Not changed, by design"). The Loop line read `WAITING ON YOU: the baseline
questions are a draft: in _eval, keep about 10 in questions.md, ...`: a folder name with nothing to find it by.
`_eval_by_name` now replaces the folder, as the loop wrote it, with `the docs repo's _eval folder`
(`_EVAL_SHOWN`), so the line reads `... are a draft: in the docs repo's _eval folder, keep about 10 in
questions.md, ...`. The line still holds no path (K16b) for any docs repo, and the Configuration part's `- docs
repo:` line gives the folder. The live wait `agentsync status` prints (`loop.py`) keeps its full path;
`loop_next_text`, `_WAIT_DRAFT` and `_stopped_wait` are unchanged (the wait's prefix is). Tests:
`test_a_draft_baseline_shows_its_wait_on_the_loop_line`,
`test_the_loop_line_keeps_no_part_of_a_docs_repo_path_with_spaces` and
`test_the_loop_line_shows_the_wait_the_loop_stopped_on_not_the_first_one`.

**The IT draft line dates the draft and names where it differs** (B13 N29; amends §16.14's Summary clause on the
IT draft and §16.15's `agentsync.it_request` interface). The line read `- IT draft: <path> exists; N field(s) left for
you (...); M left for IT` whatever wrote the draft, and a draft from an earlier agentsync told IT a User-Agent
agentsync no longer sends. After "M left for IT" it now adds, in this order:
- `; written YYYY-MM-DD`: the last `date = YYYY-MM-DD` on the draft's `Filled from this Mac:` line (above its
  first `---`; it-request's `<date>` filler). With none, `; file last changed YYYY-MM-DD`, the file's mtime as a
  UTC date; nothing if that cannot be read.
- `; differs from what `agentsync it-request --out ~/agent-context/it-request-draft.md` writes now from line N (an
  earlier agentsync wrote it, or it was edited there): unless that line is your own edit, run that command again
  before sending it; it keeps this copy as a .bak` when `first_difference` gives a line (`write_draft` keeps a
  different earlier draft as `<path>.<stamp>.bak`, so the advice loses nothing).
- `; not compared with what agentsync it-request writes now (<exception type>)` when loading the page or the
  compare raises anything: the type only, and the rest of the Summary stands (as `_loop_line`'s catch).

```python
# agentsync.it_request
def render(template: Template, facts: MacFacts, *,
           fillers: Mapping[str, Callable[[MacFacts], str | None]] = FILLERS) -> Draft: ...
def first_difference(template: Template, text: str) -> int | None: ...  # raises TemplateError
```

`first_difference` compares the email below the draft's first `---` line with `render(template, MacFacts(),
fillers={})`, line by line, line endings and trailing blanks ignored; it returns the first differing file line,
the first line past the shorter when the counts differ, 1 when the draft has no `---` line, else None. A
placeholder the page's table does not mark "leave them" matches any value on its line (in or out of its code
span): the person, the command or IT fills it, and the table lets the person change a command's value
(`<requester-name>`). A line with such placeholders matches when its literal pieces appear in order, the first at
the start and the last at the end, each middle piece at its leftmost place: linear, where a regex of them
backtracks on a long typed line. The limit: text an older draft has beyond the current page, on a line with such
a placeholder, is taken as that placeholder's value and not reported; text the page has and the draft lacks is
always found. Only a date, a line number and fixed words reach the report, never the draft's text. No command,
flag or key. Tests: `test_first_difference_matches_a_filled_draft_and_names_a_changed_line` and
`test_first_sync_doctor_warns_and_it_draft_in_the_summary`.

**Recent errors names its window** (B13 H22, bring-back 2026-10-10 C4). The report reads the last 64 KiB of each
file in the log directory (`_TAIL_BYTES`; the rotated `.log.1` and `.log.2` included, each on its own), so its count
is of the lines read, not of the whole log. When any file was longer than that, the heading says `The last <n> of
<m> WARNING/ERROR line(s) in the last 64 KiB of each log file in <log dir> ...`; otherwise it is unchanged. Whether
a file was cut comes from the same open file as its lines (`_tail_cut`), so a rotation in between cannot split the
two. Reading whole logs is not built: a job log holds up to 24 MiB (8 MiB, rotated twice), and filtering,
scrubbing and merging took about 0.9 to 2.2 s per 8 MiB of warning lines, depending on the lines (two
measurements), inside a 12 s budget that Doctor shares. A whole-log count would not be stable either: each rotation
deletes `.log.2`, so the count drops by up to a third with nothing wrong. The shell fallback's Recent errors reads
install.log's `result=failed` lines in full, so it has no window and no twin. `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md`'s
table says "log entries (repeats in a row shown once), read from the last 64 KiB of each log file". Tests:
`test_recent_errors_name_their_window` (a 3000-line log over 64 KiB names the window and counts the lines read) and
`test_recent_errors_merge_a_line_repeated_in_a_row` (a short log does not).

**Log times in the report are UTC** (B13 N10, field reports 2026-10-07 C12 and 2026-10-08 D3.f; amends §16.22: any
line of the install.out tail that starts with a log time gets that time in UTC; nothing else in it changes).
`logging` writes the Mac's local time with no zone (`cli.py` `_setup_logging`), and beside the report's UTC times
that gave the Mac's UTC offset away. The log files stay as written. `_utc_log_times` rewrites the leading
`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm` of a line in Recent errors and in the install.out tail as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ`,
read with this Mac's time zone at report time. It runs after `_scrub_item_paths`, so `_LOG_HEAD_RE` still sees the
written form, and before the merge, so the merge note's last time is UTC too; the install.out intro adds "and a
log line's local time is shown in UTC". Within one file, a time that would go back more than 1 s
(`_LOG_STEP_BACK`, milliseconds included) in the hour a fall-back repeats takes the later reading; a smaller
step back is two threads' lines written out of order and keeps its own reading, so it does not move that line,
or the lines after it, an hour on. A stamp no calendar holds (year 0001, month 13) stays as written and never fails the
section. A line whose time ends in `Z` (the launcher's) is unchanged. Limits: a line written before the Mac changed
time zone is read with the new zone; a log line quoted inside another line keeps its local stamp (the one producer
is install.sh's `warning: agentsync setup-report failed (<why>): <last output line>`, which can reach a later
report's install.out tail) (**amended 2026-10-11, §16.47 R108:** that producer's quoted time is now converted
too, by one regex anchored to its exact prefix; it does not steer the fall-back choice); the friction log is the agent's own prose and is not rewritten. The shell fallback
shows no job log and no install.out tail, so it has no twin. `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md` §4 says which times
were converted. Tests: `test_log_times_in_the_report_are_utc`, and the merge test under the `mac_zone` fixture
(America/Denver: the CI runners are in UTC, where the conversion changes nothing).

**`other` is counted by shape** (B13 N35, field triage 2026-10-08 D9.f; amends §16.30 "Quarantine names the file
types no converter reads", whose "Not done: fixed shape words" this does). Three rounds read `other 2 (1 distinct)`
and could not say whether it was a type the list lacks or a piece of a dotted name. Each unlisted suffix is now
counted by a fixed shape word (`_refused_shape`, a third SQL function on the read-only connection), read from its
text after the dot, whitespace collapsed as `_refused_type` reads it but not casefolded (casefold reads `ß` as
`ss`); only ASCII case is ignored, as SQLite's `lower` that counts D ignores it, so each distinct suffix has one
shape and the counts add up to D. The words, checked in this order: `nothing after the dot`; `with a space`; `too
long for a type` (over `_SHAPE_LONG` = 10 characters, the longest listed type's, which a test pins to the list);
`digits only` (ASCII digits: a version or a date, `v1.2`); `with a symbol` (any character but ASCII letters and
digits: a copy mark such as `.docx~`, an accent, `_`, a full-width digit); else `like a type` (1 to 10 ASCII
letters and digits with a letter). The cell reads `other N (O online-only, D distinct: n like a type, n digits
only, ...)`, shapes in the order `like a type`, `digits only`, `with a space`, `with a symbol`, `too long for a
type`, `nothing after the dot`, counts of distinct suffixes, zero counts left out, the D = 1 form too. Still one
statement and one read of `items` (a third GROUP BY column; rows are folded back per source and type in Python).
`like a type` is the shape every listed type has, and a dotted name can have it too (`jane.doe` gives `.doe`). The
other shapes are most often a name piece, a version or a copy mark, though a few real types have one (a split
archive's `.001` is digits only, `.sqlite-wal` has a symbol). No suffix or pattern of one is printed, so the rule
of §16.28 holds. Limit, as for listed types: a source label spelled like a shape word is replaced by its
placeholder. The shell fallback has no Quarantine part, so it has no twin. `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md`'s
Quarantine row names the words, and its example uses types that have no converter (`.zip`, `.dmg`). Tests:
`test_an_unlisted_suffix_is_counted_by_its_shape` (20 reasons, `ß`, the `ﬁ` ligature and full-width digits
among them), `test_like_a_type_is_as_long_as_the_longest_listed_type`,
`test_a_source_with_unlisted_suffixes_counts_them_by_shape` (six files in four shapes) and the two pins of
§16.30's tests.

**An all-zero re-read table is one line** (B13 N37, field triage 2026-10-08 D8.d; amends §16.28's "Re-read, per
local or inbox source" bullet). The last two field reports printed 16 rows of `yes`, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, `no`. When
every row would read that, the finished state, `_reread_finished` prints one line in place of the lead and the
table: `- re-read, per source: finished in all N local or inbox source(s) with a record (<labels>), and every
count of its table is 0, so the table is left out: no file from before OCR is left on this Mac for a re-read (of
the field build or not), none failed once, none was given up under this or another engine or version, and none was
being read when a cycle died.`, then the lead's sentences on the run the scan goes by (and whether it had an
engine, or "as last recorded" when no run says), on the helper, on the kinds of file counted and on a label rule.
The line names the sources the rows named, the same `labels.of` strings (at most 40, then "and K more"), so a
source with no record stays visible by its absence. Any other value in any row (`no`, `not started`, `no record`,
a count above 0, `reading when a cycle died: yes`) prints the full table, since its rows say which source; the
table's lead is unchanged byte for byte. No command, flag, config key or environment variable is added. The shell
fallback has no OCR part, so it has no twin. `docs/deploy/setup-feedback.md` names the line in its OCR row and in
the finished-state sentences. Test: `test_an_all_zero_re_read_table_is_one_line` (all finished; one `failed once`
brings every row back; an unfinished scan with every count 0 keeps the table).
Amended 2026-10-13, §16.69 H5: the line reads `- re-read, per source: finished in all N local or inbox source(s)
with a record (<labels>). Every count is 0, so the table is left out. No file on this Mac from before OCR is waiting
to be read again, from the early OCR build or not, none failed once, none was given up (under any engine or
version), and no read was cut off when a cycle died.`, and the run sentence reads "Run <id> is the newest run that
records what its re-read looked for, and `finished` is measured against it; it had an engine."

### 16.41 Installer and shell report fixes (2026-10-11, wave B13 lane D)

- **The stopped attempt's error line gives its exit code.** `install.sh --log-start` ends the step 1 error line
  of a copy it stops with `; setup stopped (exit 2)`, the exit code the prompt's error rule asks for (the
  v10 rehearsal's old-copy scenario). `_PROMPT_STOP_RE` (`agentsync.setup_report`) reads only as far as the
  reason, and the awk readers in install.sh (`friction_attempt_stopped`, `friction_earlier_end`) look for
  the fixed mark before it, so a line an earlier installer wrote, without the code, is read the same.
- **`--report-only` names the installer's own commit.** Under `install.sh --report-only` the shell fallback
  report's Summary names the installer's own checkout (`source commit <sha>`; `<sha>-dirty tree=<fp>` with
  local changes; `<sha> (local changes not checked)` when git cannot run), as `--version` does. Before, it said
  `source commit -`, because that run never reads its SOURCE. The commit is read inside
  `write_fallback_report`, only when the shell fallback writes the report, so a report agentsync writes runs no
  git for it. A real run still names its SOURCE, and its install.log start line is unchanged (`read_commit` is
  the same code moved).
- **The reinstall holds the background sync's lock** (`scripts/install.sh`, `agentsync.ops.lock`).
  - Step 2 runs `uv tool install` under `/usr/bin/lockf -k -n -s -t $AGENTSYNC_REINSTALL_WAIT_SECONDS
    <state_dir>/agentsync.lock` (default 120 s; 0 never waits), the flock(2) lock the sync takes. The lock path
    is read by the tool being replaced from the run's config (`sync_lock`, the `status_pandoc` pattern; a
    custom `[agentsync] state_dir` is honored). Without that tool, that config or that lock file (or with a
    symlinked lock, or no lockf) there is no lock and the run is today's, byte for byte.
  - A probe (`lockf -t 0 ... /usr/bin/true`, its own error line dropped) finds a running sync: then one line
    `agentsync: a background sync is running; the reinstall waits for it to end (at most <N>s)` and a ticker
    `agentsync: reinstalling after the background sync ends, still running, <N>s` at least every 15 s;
    otherwise the ticker reads `agentsync: reinstalling, still running, <N>s` (once the locked reinstall
    passes about 15 s). lockf and uv run in the foreground and the ticker beside them, as the helper builds do;
    `ticker` now takes the whole line, and the helper lines are byte-identical.
  - A background sync that starts meanwhile meets the held lock and exits 75 (skipped; launchd starts the next
    at its interval). lockf's own exit codes (64, 69, 71, 73, 75) mean it did not start uv, which never exits
    with them: then uv runs unlocked as before, after `agentsync: the background sync is still running after
    <N>s; reinstalling without waiting longer` when the wait ran out. A signalled uv (lockf 70) stays a failure.
  - **Amended 2026-10-13, §16.68 H33:** the lock does not say who started the sync, so the lines are now
    `agentsync: another sync is running (the background job, or one started in a terminal); the reinstall waits
    for it to end (at most <N>s)`, `agentsync: reinstalling after the other sync ends, still running, <N>s` and
    `agentsync: the other sync is still running after <N>s; reinstalling without waiting longer`. The install
    log's note `waited-for-a-background-sync` is a machine word the setup report reads, and stays.
  - lockf writes no body, keeps the file and its mode and never creates one, so the next sync breaks no stale
    lock that lockf left. A crashed cycle's body is kept as it was (the next sync still breaks it and runs
    FULL passes); while the reinstall holds the lock, a job, status or doctor then names that dead pid as
    the holder. This is harmless and lasts at most the wait.
  - `_describe_holder` (`agentsync.ops.lock`): a held lock with an empty body (the reinstall, an `is_held`
    probe, a cycle between flock and its write) reads `an unrecorded holder (install.sh while it reinstalls
    agentsync, or a check for an instant)`, not `'<empty body>' (unparseable lock body)`; a non-empty body
    that does not parse keeps the old text. The module docstring says so.
    **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.45 R50:** the empty-body text is now `an unrecorded holder (install.sh while it
    reinstalls agentsync, a status or doctor check, or a cycle starting)`, the same as N24's `who`, and
    doctor's held line adds `(a cycle is running)` only when the body parses as a cycle's record.
  - The setup log is unchanged: `step=agentsync seconds=N` carries the wait. The header's run-time sentence
    says a re-run may spend up to 2 minutes of the first sync's time in step 2 (the first sync would
    otherwise wait up to 600 s for the same sync). (**amended 2026-10-11, §16.47 R34:** the line now carries
    a note of what the script saw of the lock: `waited-for-a-background-sync`, `wait-ran-out-after-<N>s` or
    `lock-not-taken-rc<N>`; a run with no wait keeps the line byte for byte. The Summary's install.sh line
    shows the agentsync step's note.)
  - Why: with `--force`, uv removes and recreates the tool environment (uv 0.12.17, measured 2026-10-11:
    `bin/python`, the package and the bundled pandoc missing for 0.26 to 0.66 s of a 1.3 s reinstall, then a
    new build under any cycle still running) while a job may run from it (2026-10-08 U7; v10 E3).
  - Residuals: a cycle longer than the wait still meets the rebuild (today's behavior, said in one line); a
    job that starts inside the rebuild can fail at exec or import before it takes the lock (exit 1, as today).
    (**amended 2026-10-11, §16.47 R114, R125:** the locks are those of every config a job runs with, a locked
    install that leaves no interpreter runs once more, and a run killed with SIGKILL during the wait is said
    in the header; see §16.47.)
  - Tests: `tests/test_install_oneshot.py` (the wait, released on the first tick; a wait that runs out; no
    lock file, none created; a free lock held while uv runs; a crash marker kept; a bad
    `AGENTSYNC_REINSTALL_WAIT_SECONDS` is a usage error) and `tests/test_ops_lock.py`
    (`test_describe_names_an_empty_body_held_by_install_sh`).
- **A stop of the installer's whole process group stops the helper builds' compilers** (`ocr._run_build`, used
  by `ocr._compile` and `speech._step`).
  - Each build tool (swiftc, and for the speech helper swift package resolve, git and swift build) runs outside
    install.sh's process group, in the group of a watcher (/bin/sh, `ocr._WATCH`). The tool joins that group as
    it starts (`process_group=` the watcher's pid), so no pid is handed over.
  - The watcher ignores SIGINT itself and sends its group SIGINT when the build's Python process ends before
    the tool does: killed by any signal (SIGKILL too) or interrupted. Out of time, Python itself sends the tool
    SIGINT, and the group SIGKILL `_STOP_S` (10 s) later; TimeoutExpired is raised as before, and a tool that
    does not start still raises OSError.
  - The tool's output goes to unlinked temporary files, not pipes, read back once it ends.
  - Why: swiftc and SwiftPM start each compiler (and SwiftPM each git) in a process group of their own and stop
    them on SIGINT only. A group SIGTERM (a coding tool's timeout) left swift-driver and swift-frontend running
    for about 2 minutes, and the re-run compiled the same module beside them (B12 E1.d). It also left the
    resolve step's `git clone` running. The build's own time limit left them as well, because
    subprocess.run's SIGKILL reaches only the tool. Both tools die of SIGPIPE, so a pipe with no reader would
    kill the tool before the SIGINT reached it.
  - Not chosen: forwarding SIGINT from a Python signal handler (under SIGKILL the tool would run the rest of
    the build outside the stopped group); an exec wrapper (a tool that does not start would no longer raise
    OSError); a watcher that is told the tool's pid (Python can die before it writes the pid, and under load
    that gap was measured at milliseconds).
  - install.sh is unchanged: a signal to its pid alone still lets the build under way finish. No install.log,
    report or CLI line changes; status, doctor and sync never reach `_run_build`.
  - Tests: `tests/test_ocr.py` (`test_a_build_that_hangs_is_stopped_and_recorded`,
    `test_a_stop_of_the_whole_process_group_leaves_no_compiler_running` for SIGTERM, SIGKILL, SIGHUP and SIGINT,
    with a stub whose "compiler" outlives anything but SIGINT and which writes a line on SIGINT),
    `tests/test_speech.py` (`test_a_speech_build_out_of_time_leaves_no_compiler_running`) and
    `tests/test_ops_doctor.py` (`_run_build` among the names doctor must never reach).
- **The report install.sh writes at its own exit counts its own run's `NEXT:` as still to come** (amends
  §16.14 K17; `scripts/install.sh`, `agentsync.setup_report`).
  - `on_exit` writes the report (`write_report`) before it prints the run's `NEXT:` line, and the run's
    `# run=<id>` header is already in install.out, so the count read one `NEXT:` short ("1 NEXT: line(s) in 2
    run(s)" after two clean runs), in the Summary, the Installer section and bring-back.md's copy of it.
  - install.sh hands step 9's `agentsync setup-report` call `AGENTSYNC_REPORT_RUN=<RUN_ID>` as a prefix
    assignment inside the report's command substitution (never exported to install.sh; no other agentsync call
    sees it, though `with_timeout`'s watchdog subshell inherits it; the dry run is unchanged).
    `REPORT_RUN_ENV` names it in `agentsync.setup_report`; `_OUT_RUN_RE` captures the header's id.
  - When the last header among the lines counted carries that id, `_Facts.instructions` gets a fifth field,
    `pending`, and `_instruction_text` reads `<a> NEXT: line(s) in <r> run(s) (exactly one per install.sh run
    is expected; the run writing this report prints its NEXT: after the report, so <r-1> expected here) and
    ...`. Otherwise the text is byte-identical to before: `--report-only` (its id has no header), a run whose
    capture failed (the last header is an earlier run's), no header read, a report run by hand, an older
    agentsync (ignores the variable) or an older install.sh (sets none). The shell fallback report does not
    count install.out and is unchanged. The id is compared, never printed.
  - Not chosen: inferring the writing run from install.log (a `--no-report` run leaves the same shape and did
    print its `NEXT:`); passing the id only when a `NEXT:` is due (only an unexpected errexit leaves it empty,
    and there is no seam to test it).
  - Tests: `tests/test_setup_report.py`
    (`test_the_report_install_sh_writes_at_its_exit_expects_one_next_line_fewer`: the id of the last run, of
    an earlier run, and none) and `tests/test_install_next_line.py`
    (`test_the_report_of_each_install_run_expects_its_own_next_line_after_it`: the real setup-report through
    install.sh, two install runs and `--report-only`; bring-back.md carries the same line).
- **The shell fallback report reads past a `$'...'` word** (amends the 2026-10-10 amendment to the setup report's
  redaction, under "Redaction is on by default"). macOS's bash 3.2 `printf %q` writes a name with a byte it finds
  unprintable as `$'...'`: under a UTF-8 locale a curly apostrophe, a dash, an NFD accent or most CJK, with the
  character's first byte raw; under C every non-ASCII name, every byte in octal.
  - Before: under UTF-8 the report's exclude-list sed ran in the user's locale and stopped at that install.log
    line, so every section after the Installer tail was lost (every version since 1935b66). Under C nothing
    stopped, but no pair matched the octal text, so the Installer section showed the folder name escaped. In
    both locales a `--report-only` run with no sources.toml showed the folder in clear in the friction log
    (written before the Installer section): `read` split the word at its spaces and kept it quoted, so it never
    named a CloudStorage folder. And a word pair (a full-name token,
    the login) directly beside a non-ASCII character ended the report: macOS awk's `index`, `substr` and
    `length` are byte-wise, but its regex match under UTF-8 exits at a byte that is not UTF-8 on its own.
  - Now every stage of the shell report's filter, and of the two readers of the report it writes
    (`report_issue_link`, `friction_text`), runs byte-wise (`LC_ALL=C`); every `$'...'` word is `<path>`
    before the pairs run (install.sh logs only paths that way: `source=`, `--source-local`); and a
    `--source-local $'...'` word in install.log is unquoted (`printf %b`, after the escaped quote) into the
    folders the report redacts, through the same helper the plain words go through (`logged_source_local`).
    Coarser than `agentsync setup-report`, which keeps the path's known components; the shell report shows
    the whole word as `<path>`. Only over-redaction is added: any other `$'` in the friction text becomes
    `<path>`. The Redaction section's own text names the form in words ("every word in bash's dollar-quote
    form"), since a literal `$'` there would itself be redacted.
  - Tests: `tests/test_install_oneshot.py`: `test_the_shell_report_reads_past_a_dollar_quoted_install_log_word`
    (a curly apostrophe, an en dash, an NFD accent, and an ASCII apostrophe beside an en dash, which `%q`
    writes as `\'` inside the word, under UTF-8; an NFC accent under C),
    `test_the_shell_report_keeps_an_earlier_friction_log_past_a_stray_byte`, and the headings and issue-link
    line in `test_the_shell_report_only_redacts_the_folders_earlier_runs_added` and the `Jane’s folder` line
    in `test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_full_name_written_last_comma_first`, both under UTF-8.
- **The shell fallback report's redaction edge cases** (`scripts/install.sh`; amends the 2026-10-10 amendments
  in §16.14: the folders the shell report registers, and, under "v5 revision, redaction", the full name split at
  commas).
  - Before: a part of the full name with `*`, `?` or `[` was glob-expanded against the working directory, so
    `Jane*` became the names of matching files there (`Janet-notes.txt`), and the part itself was not a pair. A configured generic component (`Documents`) matched inside other words
    (`MyDocuments` became `My<folder-1>`). A value matched inside a placeholder an earlier value wrote, or one
    already in the text: a folder named `name` gave `<<folder-1>>`, and the Redaction note's own words were
    replaced (`the login <folder-1> (<user>)`). A configured folder named like a heading word redacted the
    heading (`## Agent friction <folder-1>`, which the next `--report-only` looks for when friction.md is
    missing). And a `--source-local` word in install.log written `~/...` or relative was never placed, so a
    `--report-only` run showed its folder names in clear.
  - Now the full name's parts are split without glob expansion. A configured CloudStorage component that is
    one of `setup_report._GENERIC_FOLDERS` is redacted as a whole word, as the Python report matches it (a test
    keeps the shell's `generic_folder` list equal to that set); any other component is still a substring. No
    value is replaced inside a placeholder an earlier value wrote, as in the Python report's single pass (**amended
    2026-10-11, §16.49, R43:** the Python report's Summary item lines are redacted twice, once before they are cut
    and then with the whole report, so before §16.46 R69 a registered value could still match inside a
    placeholder the first pass wrote, `<<folder-1>-1>`; R69 has the Redactor hold a placeholder's shape first),
    nor
    inside a report or it-request.md placeholder already in the text (the friction log of an earlier report:
    `<name>`, `<user>`, `<host>`, `<mdmhost>`, `<tmp>`, `<path>`, `<serial>`, `<org>`, `<Org>`, `<team>`,
    `<TEAMID>`, and `<org-N>`, `<folder-N>` and the other numbered kinds); the Python report does not hold the
    latter. The filter runs byte-wise (`LC_ALL=C`). The shell report's headings are never redacted, and its
    Redaction section is written after redaction, as the issue link is. A `--source-local` word read from
    install.log is placed as install.sh placed it (`~` is the home); a relative word is placed only when it
    names CloudStorage or one of its entries (install.log records no working directory; a `.` or `..` first part
    never does, though `$cs/..` exists), and otherwise the
    argument as logged (`./` kept) is shown as `--source-local <path>`, never the bare word, which may be a
    common one (`docs`). A `$'...'` word is placed only whole, once unquoted, never as the still-quoted
    pieces `read` splits it into at its spaces.
  - Stated, not built: friction-log prose naming a relative folder install.log cannot place stays in clear (the
    shell lists nothing inside a provider, for the File Provider privacy prompt); a distinctive configured
    name stays a substring pair (`log` still gives `install.<folder-1>` in body text).
  - Tests: `tests/test_install_oneshot.py`: `test_the_shell_report_does_not_glob_a_name_part`,
    `test_the_shell_folder_list_is_the_python_reports_generic_set`,
    `test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_generic_configured_folder_as_a_whole_word`,
    `test_the_shell_report_never_redacts_inside_a_placeholder` (also the note's words and a copied
    `<mdmhost>`), `test_the_shell_report_reads_tilde_and_relative_folders_from_install_log` (the words as bash
    3.2's `printf %q` logs them, `./`, `../` and `./../` included), and `test_the_shell_report_never_redacts_its_own_headings`
    (`Status`, `log`).

### 16.42 Converters and speech (2026-10-11, wave B13 lane E)

#### A PDF picture is read the way up the page shows it (N45)

Amends §16.26 ("Its stored pixels are read"). With an engine, `PdfConverter` turns and flips a picture's
stored pixels the way up a viewer shows it before the helper reads it: `_shown(obj, rotation)` takes the
image's matrix, the matrix of each form around it and the page's `/Rotate`, snaps the directions of the
stored columns and rows to the nearest screen axis, and `_png(bitmap, shown)` writes the picture in that
orientation, a row at a time, with no imaging library. One of the eight turns and flips; a picture drawn a
little askew is read the quarter-turn nearest; one at 45 degrees, skewed to no area, or whose matrix cannot
be read is read as stored. A page whose `/Rotate` cannot be read counts as not turned; `MemoryError` is
never taken for either failure, it fails the pass. A page image is rendered by PDFium with its `/Rotate` as
before, and `_png(bitmap)` writes it byte for byte as before. A picture is known by (stream sha256, pixel
size, orientation), so one stream drawn two ways is two pictures, each charged its pixels; one drawn the
same way on every page is still decoded once. `ocr_pdf_rules` is 3. No version, no helper, no key of a Mac
without an engine moves. A page already published is not read again for this: it keeps its reading until
its file changes (as with the bump to 2). Measured with the real helper: a screenshot stored a quarter
right and drawn upright read as one merged line in reverse order before, as its two lines now; one stored
bottom-up (drawn with a negative `d`) was mirrored and unreadable before, and is read now.

The other way round is now the limit: a picture stored upright and drawn turned, so that the page itself
shows it on its side (a wide table turned to fit a portrait page, a browser's CSS-turned image), is read
on its side, as a page without a text layer always was. Vision still reads its words; its lines come back
merged. Measured on a Chrome-printed and a WebKit-printed page: three table rows read as three lines
before, as one line now. The file cannot tell the two cases apart (both are a wide stored picture shown
tall); only the text in it can. The page's way up is taken because browsers (Chrome, WebKit) embed every
portrait phone photo the first way, its EXIF turn applied by the matrix, and because a mirrored or
upside-down picture, which nobody draws that way on purpose, was not read at all. Pictures in a deck or
Word file drawn with a `rot` or flip are still read as stored (their embedded JPEG's EXIF is honoured by
the helper).

Amended 2026-10-11 by §16.48 (R82): a picture stored upright and drawn turned is no longer read on its
side. A quarter-turned picture whose lines come back running down is read once more the other way, and
that reading is kept when its lines run across. `ocr_pdf_rules` is 4.

Every new name in `agentsync.convert.pdf` is private (`_shown`, `_screen_axis`, `_Axes`, `_UPRIGHT`).

Tests: `tests/test_convert_formats.py` (a picture drawn upright, turned, flipped, inside a turned form and
on a turned page, against PDFium's own drawing of the page; one drawn askew, at 45 degrees and with no
area; a turned picture through the converter, and one stream drawn two ways; a `/Rotate` that cannot be
read, and memory running out while it is read; `ocr_pdf_rules` 3) and `tests/test_ocr.py` (the real helper
reads a picture stored on its side as its two lines). `build_picture_pdf(…, rotate=)` in
`tests/test_convert_builders.py` writes the page's `/Rotate`.

#### Internet shortcuts (H24)

Amends §7's routing and §16.26's setup-report scrub. `.url` → `text-plain`: the file is fenced as `ini`,
whole, so `IconFile=` and the like stay visible. The page's title is the file's name (the converter leaves
the title empty and `publish` fills in the shown name, as for a picture) and its summary is `Internet
shortcut to <target>` or `Internet shortcut with no URL`. The target is the first `URL=` line with an `=`
under `[InternetShortcut]`; the section name and the key are matched without case, spaces around either
are dropped, a line with no `=` is skipped as Windows skips it, and a `URL=` under any other section
(`[InternetShortcut.W]`, the property-store section) does not count. Output for every other suffix is
byte for byte what it was, so the emitter version stays 1.0.0; the action key carries the suffix, and a
refusal is never cached, so no cached entry is stale. An existing `no converter for .url` stub becomes a
page with no operator step: on this Mac through the re-read pass (the registry's suffixes are part of its
capabilities), online-only through the work queue under the byte budget. A URL holding a secret is caught
by the secret scan and the page is a `contains a credential` stub. Like a `.txt`, a `.url` carries no
sensitivity label, so label exclusions do not apply to it. A shortcut that is not text (NUL bytes: UTF-16
with no BOM) is a failed conversion, as any such text file is. `.webloc` and `.website` are still refused.

`_PATH_IN_LOG_RE` gains `url`, so a warning that names a shortcut at a source's top is `<path>` in the
report; routing `.url` without it would put the file's name in Recent errors. It also gains `m4v`, the
one suffix of the recording converter it lacked (a leak that was there before this item), and
the per-suffix test now takes `RecordingConverter.extensions` beside the registry's and the image
converter's (amends §16.26's test list): 36 suffixes. `.url` stays in `_REFUSED_TYPE_LIST`, since a stub
can be older than its converter.

Tests: `tests/test_convert_formats.py` (a plain shortcut; one with the property-store section first, a
lower-case section and a spaced key; one with `URL=` only under another section; one with a bare `URL`
line before the real one), `tests/test_convert_core.py` (the pinned route set), `tests/test_cycle.py` (a
stub from before the converter is read once as a page, and not again) and `tests/test_setup_report.py`
(a log line naming a file of each claimed suffix is scrubbed).

#### Outlook messages through olefile (N46)

Amends §7's routing, §14 item 8 and the content-policy re-screen list. `Registry.default` routes `.msg` to
`msg-olefile` (`agentsync.convert.msg.MsgConverter`) unless `policy.labels_active`: a `.msg` holds its
sensitivity label in a named MAPI property that `policy.read_labels` does not read, so any label rule
keeps the `no converter for .msg` stub (plan D8, as for images). A reader written by hand that missed one
place a label can sit would publish an excluded message; keeping the converter out cannot. `.msg` joins
`cycle._LABEL_CAPABLE`, so a page published before a rule is re-screened into that stub, and a `.msg`
that arrives under a rule is not fetched. No purge is queued, because no label was read: the page's
earlier text stays in history, as for an image (§16.26). The converter needs no engine, so a caller of
`Registry.default` that leaves `policy` out reads every `.msg`; the cycle, its only caller, passes the
effective policy. **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.61 F81 (by §16.54 Q78):** under a label rule `.msg` goes to `msg-mime`,
so every `.msg` is fetched; a MIME one is screened and read as an `.eml`, and only a binary one keeps the `no
converter for .msg` stub and the re-screen into it. **Amended 2026-10-12, §16.60 F73:** one that reading means
a download for (online-only, a Graph item, a refused hydration) is still refused by its name.

The page has the `.eml` shape. The header table is From, To, Cc, Date, Subject, Message-ID, In-Reply-To
and References, from MAPI properties. From is the sent-representing party (0x0042 with 0x5D02, else
0x0065), which is what an `.eml`'s From header holds, so mail from a shared mailbox or a delegate names
the mailbox; else the sender (0x0C1A with 0x5D01, else 0x0C1F). An address with no `@` (an Exchange
