an option) and `test_setup_report_form_has_a_run_type` (the options are `FORM_OUTCOME_OPTIONS`).

**A git URL rewrite's host and path are redacted, in both reports** (H20; dated line at §16.46 Proxies). v15's git
stop names a URL rewrite as a cause, and with `url."https://<mirror>/".insteadOf = https://github.com/` git's error
names the mirror (`Could not resolve host: <mirror>`), which both reports printed in clear: only proxies were
registered. Both readers now read `[url "<base>"]` sections with an `insteadOf` key (never `pushInsteadOf`) from the
files they read git's proxies from (`~/.gitconfig`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config`, `/etc/gitconfig`, the two
checkouts' repository configs), as files, with no git process: on a Mac without the developer tools `/usr/bin/git`
opens the install dialog, and that is the step 1 stop in which the report runs. Python: `_git_rewrite_bases`, sharing
`_git_config_names` with `_git_proxy_urls`; shell: `git_rewrite_bases`, sharing `git_config_files` with
`git_proxy_values`, every pipeline stage under `LC_ALL=C`. A base is a URL (`https://user@host:port/path/`) or git's
scp form (`git@host:path`); a base whose host is `github.com`, in any case and form, is skipped, so the repository
locator and the issue link stay whole (registering it would have made GitHub `<proxy-N>`). For each other base its
host is registered as a proxy host is (a dotless generic host only inside a URL), then the base after its scheme and
user, as the PAC value is, so a company word in its path goes too (`dev.example/<org>/` would otherwise read
`<proxy-1>/<org>/`), and for the scp form its path with the leading `:`: the Python redactor matches `user@host` as
an email address before any value, so a printed `git@host:path` kept its path otherwise. A URL base's path is not a
value of its own (its base value covers it), nor is an scp path of a server's generic words only (`git`, `scm`,
`repos`: `_GENERIC_PATH_WORDS`, and the report's own words in Python), which would cut `/usr/bin/git` and a
`github.com` link (a reviewer's measurement); the shell matches the path as a whole word (pair flag `w`). The shell
also adds each value's lower-case form, since its pairs are case-sensitive and a resolver error prints the host in
lower case, and registers the base before the host, as it does the PAC value, so its `<proxy-N>` numbers can differ
from the Python report's. All are `<proxy-N>`, registered after git's proxies and before the LaunchAgent's, so no
existing `<proxy-N>` is renumbered and no placeholder class or legend changes. The Environment line adds a count, `URL rewrite in git's config: set (N)` or `not set`. Tests:
`tests/test_setup_report.py::test_a_git_url_rewrite_host_and_path_are_redacted` (with no git on PATH),
`tests/test_install_oneshot.py::test_the_shell_report_redacts_a_git_url_rewrite_host_and_path`.

**Two round 6 tests pin what they claim** (H45; tests only). In
`test_a_context_organisation_is_matched_only_after_an_app_name_and_only_for_a_generic_word` the `word_named_shown`
assert sat after the loop over Status, Probe, Stage, Context and Agent, so it checked Agent alone; it is inside the
loop now. `test_the_on_origin_main_line_dates_the_checkouts_last_fetch` never gave the worktree a FETCH_HEAD of its
own, so "the newer of the two" (G27) compared one file; the worktree now fetches too, and each file is made the
newer in turn. Measured: replacing `max(stats, key=st_mtime)` with the first or the last file found fails the test.

### 16.70 Round 7: installer and the shell report (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 7 lane RB)

Round 7 findings (`round7/items/H<n>.md` of the bring-back cache) built in `scripts/install.sh`, each with a test in
`tests/test_install_oneshot.py`.

- **Step 1's synced-folder reader runs on the agentsync an earlier setup left** (H7; H15, H27 and H38 are the
  same defect). `--list-folders` runs `synced_folders` through the installed agentsync's interpreter, and step 2
  is what updates that agentsync. Round 6 (§16.63 G39) had the reader import `agentsync.paths.provider_link_resolved`
  bare. No agentsync installed before 2026-10-13 has that name, so on every Mac set up earlier the import failed,
  no folder was marked, no `already synced on this Mac:` line was printed, and an unattended agent stopped at the
  folder question. The import now sits in `try` / `except ImportError`, and the fallback is the same single
  `readlink` of the provider entry written with `os` and `pathlib` alone: it uses no other agentsync name
  (`cloud_storage_roots` and `cloud_relative` date from 2026-10-12, so a fallback built on them would fail on a
  Mac set up between 2026-09-29 and then). Only ImportError is caught: a config that does not load still reaches
  the warning. Measured with the agentsync of `53824b3b` (2026-09-29), `4a42af93`, `cebf2775` and this build: the
  same marks from all four, a folder stored through a provider link included.
  **The rule for the next name:** the reader may import `load_config` and `canonical_source_root` from
  `agentsync.config` with no guard; any other agentsync name is imported in a `try` whose `except ImportError`
  defines it with the standard library alone. `test_the_synced_folder_reader_imports_no_agentsync_name_an_older_build_lacks`
  parses the reader and fails on an import outside that rule;
  `test_list_folders_marks_the_synced_folders_with_an_agentsync_from_before_round_6` runs the list with an
  agentsync that lacks the name.
- **The warning names its cause in fixed words** (H14 and H16, one defect; H27's half of H7). The line is
  `warning: could not read which folders <config> already syncs (<cause>), so none is marked below`, and the
  cause is one of four, checked in this order: `no agentsync is installed`; `the reader took over 10 s`; `the
  installed agentsync is older than this installer (it has no <name>)`, where `<name>` is the identifier from
  the reader's `cannot import name '<name>'` line; `the installed agentsync could not load it`. The reader's
  stderr was thrown away before, and the one text, "no installed agentsync loads it", was false on a Mac that
  has one. Nothing else of what the reader wrote is printed: an error line can quote the config, and an agent
  copies a warning into the friction log. The prefix and the suffix are unchanged.
  `test_list_folders_says_why_an_installed_agentsync_could_not_run_the_reader`,
  `test_list_folders_marks_nothing_when_the_config_cannot_be_read`.

### 16.71 Round 7: converters and the .msg re-read (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 7 lane E)

Builds round 7's `.msg` re-screen, QUARANTINE.tsv, tombstone and convert-docstring items, and the timing-test skip
(`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 7"; specs `round7/items/H<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built).
As in §16.66, a line that corrects §16.66 is here; the dated lines are the two H77's spec names.

**A policy tweak that keeps the label rule reads no withheld `.msg` again (H47; corrects §16.66 G52).**
`Manifest.mark_for_rescreen` takes `unread_only`, and `_check_policy_change` sets it while the new policy has a label
rule on: a refused `no converter for <suffix>` row is marked only when no byte of it was read (no content hash). G52
marked every such row, a binary `.msg` read on this Mac under the rule included, so a tweak that kept the rule on
(a second label id) read each one again, and the sync line counted them as converted and refused but not as
re-screened. Once the rule is lifted every such row is marked, as G52 built, a read one that has since gone
online-only included; marking only unread rows always would leave that one's stub for good. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_policy_tweak_that_keeps_the_label_rule_reads_no_binary_msg_again` and
`test_a_binary_msg_read_under_the_rule_then_online_only_is_read_once_the_rule_is_lifted` (the guard against the
narrower fix); `test_under_a_label_rule_a_refused_image_is_not_read_and_without_the_rule_it_is` stays green.

**QUARANTINE.tsv copies the reason of the stub as published (H52; corrects §16.66 G29's last sentence).**
`write_quarantine` no longer reads this run's OCR state. For a refused row a label rule may withhold (a rule on,
its suffix in `label_withheld_suffixes()`, its stored reason `no converter for <suffix>`) it copies the `reason:` of
the row's page (`Publisher._stub_reason`) when it is one of the two wordings, and otherwise keeps the stored reason.
Whether an image's stub says `withheld by label rule` is decided by the run that planned it; the TSV, rewritten every
run, followed each run's engine, so a run whose engine missed its `--version` made a TSV-only commit contradicting
the page, and an engine that arrived after the stub left the two disagreeing for good. Re-planning stubs when the
engine flaps would turn each flap into a page commit, so it is not done. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_quarantine_tsv_keeps_the_wording_of_the_published_stub_whatever_this_runs_ocr` (engine
on, on, off, off, on; and off, then on: one commit, page and TSV equal after every run).

**The no-converter docstrings (H56).** `NO_CONVERTER_PREFIX` says its stub's stored reason keeps the prefix while a
withheld stub's page, `reason:` and TSV row show `withheld by label rule: ...`; `label_withheld_suffixes()` says an
image counts as withheld only while an OCR engine is ready, and names a `.msg` the OS refused to hydrate. Docstrings
only.

**A re-rendered tombstone with no `last_commit` names the commit that holds its content (H77; amends §16.60 F68,
§16.66 G77).** Compaction leaves a tombstone row with no `last_commit` (its commit squashed; the page keeps the
dangling sha), and G77's rewrite rendered "pick the commit before this tombstone", though the rewrite is itself a
tombstone commit, so that commit opened the older tombstone. `Cycle._rerender_tombstones` first stores in the row
the newest commit on the path whose page is not `status: deleted` (`_content_commit`: `git log --format=%H` and
`cat-file`, read-only), so the page gets an exact `git show` line and later repair and unarchive renders agree. With
none in history the page is still rewritten, banner first: skipping it would keep a third-party title above the
banner (§16.51 Q9) for no working line. That line now reads "pick the newest commit whose page is not a tombstone,
status: deleted", true after repair and unarchive commits too. `STUB_RENDER` is 5 (corrects §16.66's "is 4"), so an
install at 4 renders once more. Dated lines at §16.60 F68 and §16.66 G77. Pinned by
`tests/test_cycle.py::test_a_tombstone_with_no_last_commit_is_rendered_again_with_the_commit_that_holds_its_content`
(content kept; squashed to one root commit).

**A timing test reads the load when it starts (H78).** `tests/conftest.py` skips a `timing` test in
`pytest_runtest_setup`, not once at collection: under `-n auto` each worker collects at startup, so a long run whose
load rose later still ran them (a 6 s bound failed at 34 per core). Same threshold (4 per core) and
`AGENTSYNC_TIMING=1` override. Pinned by `tests/test_perf.py::test_a_timing_test_reads_the_load_when_it_starts`.

### 16.72 Round 7: setup prompt v16 (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 7 lane P)

The B13 round 7 items of lane P (specs `round7/items/H<n>.md`, the verifier's corrected fix built). All ten need
prompt text (H6, H9, H19, H21, H25, H26, H30, H65, H66, H70), so the prompt is **setup prompt v16**:
`SETUP_PROMPT_COMPAT`, `PROMPT_VERSION`, step 1's `prompt v16` and `setup-prompt-compat 16`, the issue form's
placeholder and the block's digest move together; a saved v15 copy is stopped at step 1 like every older copy. v16
moves no step, so it has no `PROMPT_LAYOUTS` entry and is read with v7's rules. None adds an agentsync command, an
installer flag, a config key or a friction kind. This section amends the older sections it names here; the older
text stays as the record of its version.

**The finish's folder list is the config's** (H9 and H30, one defect, built once; amends §16.36 and §16.43's
finish). v15 listed "those step 1's list marked [synced] and those step 2 added", with `sources.toml` only for a
step 1 that stopped before its list. The list can run to its end and mark nothing (an installed agentsync too old
for the reader's import, §16.70; the reader's 10 s timeout; a config the installed tool cannot load), and step 2
then prints `folders: kept the N already synced (none added)`, so the literal answer was a false "none: this Mac
syncs no folder". The finish now reads "the kind = "local" sources in ~/agent-context/sources.toml that are not
paused or retired, read after step 2 or, if setup stopped before step 2, as they are (never the inbox or another
kind = "inbox" folder), saying which of them this session added: those for which a run of step 2 this session
printed an "added source" line; or, if sources.toml has no such kind = "local" source, "none: this Mac syncs no
folder"". "Added" is add-source's own per-folder line (`added source '<id>' to <config>:`, printed only when it
writes the folder), which step 2's `add_source_filter` passes on; the `folders:` line gives counts only, so H30's
"as many as step 2's folders: line says" could not name the paths. H9's verifier keyed on the absence of the
`already configured:` line instead; the lane's review measured that a re-run of step 2 (which the prompt allows)
prints that line for every folder the first run added, so the positive line is the one built. Rejected: making step
2 refuse an already-configured `--source-local` (exit 2 ends setup before install on the Mac where the reader
fails, H9's verifier) and a second "already synced, not added" line (`already configured:` is that line). Test:
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_step3_runs_the_loop_then_the_report`).

**At the folder wait the NEXT item is "none"** (H6; amends §16.43's H3 paragraph, "The finish names one NEXT
line"). Step 3 lists the folder wait as a case with no report, so "the last NEXT: line printed before the report"
pointed at a report that never ran, while `--list-folders` had printed a NEXT: line that names install.sh with the
folder left open. The item now adds "(also "none: waiting for your folder answer" while you wait for my folder
answer in step 1; the folder list's NEXT: line is not a step for me)". Test: as H9.

**The keep command keeps a local commit and moves main to the update** (H19; amends §16.30's "The bring-back sends
local work once"). A checkout with a local commit behind origin fails the pull with "Not possible to fast-forward",
which the prompt did not call local changes; v15's keep command then failed at its commit ("nothing to commit",
exit 1) and left the checkout on its new branch with no upstream, so every later paste's pull said "no tracking
information" and got the network message (measured, git 2.54, a throwaway home). Step 1 now names git's words for
both kinds ("would be overwritten", "Not possible to fast-forward"), and the command is `... switch -c
local-work-<time> && ... add -A && { ... diff --cached --quiet || ... commit ...; } && ... format-patch -q
origin/main.. -o ~/agent-context/setup/local-work && ... fetch origin && ... switch -C main origin/main`, led by
`... merge-base --is-ancestor main HEAD &&`: it commits only what is staged, writes one patch per commit the update
lacks, and resets main to the update only after the branch and the patches exist (the old tip stays on the branch).
The leading check is the lane review's: on a checkout that is not on main, with a commit on main the checked-out
branch lacks, the reset left that commit on no branch and in no patch (measured); the check stops the command
first, exit 1 with no output and nothing changed, and the prompt sends that case, with "no tracking information",
to `git switch main` and step 1 again, where the keep runs from main. When only the fetch or the switch failed, the
prompt names those two to run again; a checkout already left on a branch runs `git -C ~/src/agent-context-sync
switch main` first. The Rules line's exception reads "keeping local changes on a branch and moving main to the
update, as step 1 says, is none of these", since `-C` resets a branch. §16.30's "Not by file name" paragraph now
holds for the commit of uncommitted changes only: a local commit's patch is named `NNNN-<its subject>.patch`, and a
second keep overwrites a first keep's patch only where both get the same number and subject; the section 3 reader
loops over every `*.patch` in name order and decides by each one's mtime whether to send it, so nothing there
changes. Tests: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_keeps_a_local_commit_and_moves_main_to_the_update`,
`test_the_keep_command_leaves_a_main_with_commits_of_its_own_as_it_is`,
`test_a_checkout_a_v15_keep_left_on_its_branch_goes_back_to_main`,
`test_readme_keeps_local_work_then_runs_step_1_again`, `test_step1_keeps_local_changes_on_a_branch_and_updates`).

**The git stop's quote is sentences, and its rewrite query is anchored** (H21, H25; amends §16.67's G73 paragraph).
The quote was one 106-word sentence, 86 words of it one parenthesis nesting three sources, with the one action
after all of it. It now reads "A corporate proxy may need HTTPS_PROXY set in your terminal. If git's error names a
host other than github.com, git was told to use that host in one of three ways, and any of them may point at a
network this Mac is not on: a URL rewrite, which `git config --get-regexp '^url\..*\.insteadof$'` prints; git's own
proxy setting, which `git config --get-urlmatch http.proxy https://github.com` prints and which wins over the
terminal's; or the terminal's HTTPS_PROXY, https_proxy, ALL_PROXY or all_proxy, which `env | grep -i proxy` shows.
Once git can reach GitHub from a terminal, start a new session from that terminal and paste this prompt again". The
unanchored `'url\..*insteadof'` also printed `url.<base>.pushinsteadof`, which never changes a fetch or pull URL
(measured: `git remote get-url origin` resolved to the insteadOf host, only `--push` to the pushInsteadOf one); git
lower-cases the key name, so the anchored query keeps every insteadOf, whatever its case. Test:
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_step1_is_one_command`).

**One `## Not used` line after a stop before step 2** (H26). Before step 2 no part of agentsync has run, so the
line per part was twelve copies of one reason. Step 3 adds, after "saying why", "(if setup stopped before step 2,
no part was used: one line saying so and naming the step it stopped at is enough)". Only that case shares a line:
in any other session the per-part reasons are what triage reads. Test: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_prompt_routes_changes_to_the_source_not_the_checkout`).

**The checkout sentence follows any error that does not name the checkout** (H65; amends §16.67's G15/G67
paragraph). Installers v8 to v14 answer a newer copy with "Tell the person to copy the prompt again" (measured on
trees at their commits), so v15's "tell me that, in its words" relayed only that, and the checkout sentence,
reached only with no such error, never came for the checkout that follows a fork, the case it was written for. Step
1 now reads "When step 1 stops here, if the command's error says what to tell me, tell me that, in its words;
otherwise (--version printed another number and no such error), tell me to copy the prompt again from README.md on
the main branch of the Source above. Either way, unless the error's words already mention this Mac's checkout, also
tell me that if a fresh copy stops here too, this Mac's checkout (~/src/agent-context-sync) does not follow main of
the Source: point it there, or move it aside so step 1 clones it, then paste the prompt again." A v15 or later
installer's error for a newer copy names the checkout (`newer_copy_fix`), so it is relayed alone. Test: as H70.

**A changed `--log-start` value runs step 1 once more** (H70). The installer's error ends, for every copy, "If the
first line of your prompt says "setup prompt vN", the --log-start value was changed: run step 1's command again",
while the stop said to run no other step. An exception keyed on that sentence would match every mismatched copy too
(the verifier's measured objection: each rerun closes another attempt in the friction log). It keys on the
installer's number instead: "But if the error says this installer is for v16, this prompt's own number, the copy
matches and only step 1's command was changed: run it again once, exactly as written here, and stop as above if it
stops the same way again." A copy that does not match never meets an installer for its own number. Step 3's
no-report case reads "when step 1 stops (after at most that one rerun) because this prompt is not the installer's",
and install.sh's sentence now says "run step 1's command again once, exactly as the prompt writes it". The words
avoid "setup prompt v16" and "--log-start", which the block holds once each by test. Tests:
`tests/test_deploy_pack.py` (`test_readme_prompt_names_its_version_and_the_installer_compat_line`,
`test_readme_report_step_after_any_failure`).

**The first sync's wait is its own sentence** (H66; amends §16.67's G37 paragraph). The installer probes the
config's lock before its first sync every time ("step 2's wait ran out, or one started since"), and a re-run at the
same commit reinstalls nothing, so v15's "its first sync then says ... waits for that sync again, up to 10 more
minutes" covered only one of the cases. Step 2 now has two sentences: the reinstall's wait, then "If another sync
is running when its first sync starts (that same one, or one that started since, such as a background sync on a Mac
that already syncs), it says "another sync is still running" and waits for it, up to 10 minutes, and skips that
sync ("skipped, lock busy") if it is still running then." Test: `tests/test_deploy_pack.py`
(`test_readme_step2_is_the_one_install_command`).

### 16.73 Round 7: deploy docs and CONTRACTS cross-references (2026-10-13, wave B13 round 7 lane D)

Docs and dated lines that lagged round 6's code (`docs/plans/bring-back-ocr.md`, "B13 round 7"); no behavior
changes. Each item is pinned by a test in `tests/test_deploy_pack.py` that fails on the text it replaced.

**A withheld `.msg`'s QUARANTINE.tsv row reads as the code writes it** (H53, H59: one defect). Since §16.66 G29 a
`.msg` a label rule withholds has `withheld by label rule: ...` (`publish._withheld_reason`) as its page's
`reason:` and as its `_sync/QUARANTINE.tsv` reason, also for one withheld without a download; data-governance.md
still said the QUARANTINE.tsv reason stays `no converter for .msg`, which is now only the stored reason. Test:
`test_the_docs_state_the_msg_purge_and_banner_rules_of_round_4`.

**The stopped outcome and the title's step name are in the reviewer's guide** (H43, H61, H67: one defect; dated
line at §16.64 G12). setup-feedback.md's computed outcomes had no `stopped at step 1 (<note>)` (§16.64 G23), and its
`Failed at step N` fallback and agent-friction sentence called such an attempt failed; a fourth bullet gives the
whole condition (no install run, no error, no end line, every line a step 1 deviation), both notes and the form's
`Failed at step 1 (preflight)`. The `title` row said the title holds the outcome; since §16.64 G12 it names the
step as the attempt's own prompt does, while the `outcome` field takes the form's option (since §16.69 H11 the same
words for step 3; v7's step 2 `install` and a v5 step still map to the option for the same work), and since §16.69
H42 a stopped attempt's title reads `Stopped at step 1 (preflight)`. Test:
`test_setup_feedback_states_the_report_rules_of_round_6`.

**A label-escalation entry stays queued while its file is published, in both guides** (H58, H63). Since §16.62
G30, `governance.KEPT_REASONS` holds `label-escalation` as well as `upstream-deleted`: a run of the queue skips such
an entry while the label policy publishes its file again (live or online-only), its preview says so in its own
`note: stays queued:`, and the run's K counts both reasons. setup-feedback.md's Purge queue row said an entry with
another reason is erased and listed only the upstream deletion as kept; it now names both, and DLP, erasure and
operator entries as the ones still erased. data-governance.md's labels item says the entry stays queued, is skipped
while the file is published, runs if the policy refuses the file again, and that `agentsync purge path=<its path>
--source <its source> --reason label-escalation` erases it anyway; the purge-queue item names its kept entry as an
`upstream-deleted` one. Test: `test_the_docs_say_a_label_escalation_entry_stays_queued_while_its_file_is_published`.

**The `<org-N>` row gives the generic-word rule, and the generic-folder exception is stated** (H60). The row said
any one-word organisation the report prints is replaced only in the folder names; since §16.64 G45, G46 and G75
that holds for the reviewed generic words of `setup_report._CONTEXT_ORG_WORDS` only, and any other report word
(`Status`) is replaced everywhere and makes the report Private only. The paragraph under the table now says that a
configured folder or library named as every cloud drive's (`_GENERIC_FOLDERS`, §16.64 G48) leaves either report
public. The doc gives examples, not the lists: a third copy would have no test keeping it equal. Test:
`test_the_placeholder_table_states_the_org_word_and_generic_folder_rules_of_round_6`, which checks each example
against the lists.

**The `<proxy-N>` row gives one rule for both reports** (H62; dated line at §16.65 G4). The row and G4 said the
agentsync report replaces a common-word proxy host only inside a URL; its url mode also matches one before
`:<port>`, as the shell report does, so the row now says "only where a URL or `host:port` names it, in both
reports". The module docstring already gave that rule; the inner docstrings that say "only where a URL names it"
are left to their lanes (comments only). Test: `test_the_proxy_row_gives_one_rule_for_both_reports`.

**A header is any of the four friction keys** (H64; dated lines at §16.58 F23 and §16.67 G64). setup-feedback.md,
the §16.58 F23 line §16.67 G64 wrote and §16.67's own bullet defined a header as a `Prompt:` or `Agent:` line, while
`setup_report.FRICTION_KEYS` (and install.sh's `track()`) also count an `Outcome:` or `Run:` line, as §16.64 G51
says: such a line splits an attempt exactly as `Prompt:` does (measured with `parse_friction`). Both passages now
name the four, with the last two marked as a v4 log's. Test: `test_setup_feedback_states_the_report_rules_of_round_4`,
whose `parse_friction` loop now runs an `Outcome:` and a `Run:` header too.

**The banner re-render names the tombstones it covers** (H68). `Cycle._rerender_stubs` runs the tombstone pass for

tombstone of a source deleted from sources.toml (allowed once its rows are all tombstones) keeps the old layout until

names the exception. Test: `test_the_banner_re_render_names_the_tombstones_it_covers`.

**The Send step counts five values** (H71). The issue link fills `setup_report.ISSUE_FIELDS`, five since

**The newer-copy paragraph quotes the Summary's cause** (H72). Since §16.64 G20 the agentsync report's Summary names
